News.title: Man goes missing at popular lake as urgent search launched just 11 days after another body was pulled from water
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FIND HIM Man goes missing at popular lake as urgent search launched just 11 days after another body was pulled from water

POLICE have launched a search after a man has gone missing at a popular UK lake.

Emergency services were called to Llyn Geirionydd lake in Wales at around 7.10pm on Sunday.



Police helicopters and divers have reportedly been seen scouring the area find the man.

One witness said that there was a “significant emergency response” as search teams spent the night looking for the missing person.



Llyn Geirionydd is a 45-acre lake nestled on the lower slopes of the Carneddau mountains in Snowdonia.

North Wales Police said that the man’s family has been notified as it continues in its search.



It has told the public to avoid the area as emergency services continue with their work.

The body of a 21-year-old man had recent been recovered from the lake just 11 days ago.

News.title: ‘Shocked’ new mum gives birth to one of Britain’s biggest babies – with newborn already wearing clothes for 6-month-olds
News.content:
TITAN TOT ‘Shocked’ new mum gives birth to one of Britain’s biggest babies – with newborn already wearing clothes for 6-month-olds

A MUM has given birth to one of Britain’s biggest babies.

Jenallie Ross, 33, had a C-section earlier this month for her son, who weighs 14 pounds and 2 ounces.



The baby, still unnamed, was just shy of Britain’s heaviest baby who weighed a staggering 15lb 8 oz.

He is already wearing clothes for a three to six month old baby despite being just days old.



And he is going through two bottles worth of milk with Jenallie expecting him to keep growing at a rapid pace.

Jenallie, 33, said: “I couldn’t believe it. I was crying. The first thing I said was ‘where did this big baby come from – he’s so big!’.



“But my tummy was really big – it was really rough carrying him.

“I had to have extra ultrasounds every two weeks to check his growth. The pounds just kept packing on.

“They couldn’t figure out why he was growing so big.

“They told me I had to have a C-section. I didn’t want surgery. I cried so much.



“I had to have extra ultrasounds every two weeks to check his growth. The pounds just kept packing on. They kept doing tests, maybe it was genetic.

“I was scared. I suffered with my blood sugar levels.”

Janallie is 5’7 and the baby’s dad Victor Okanme, 26, is 6ft.

The baby weighed double the weight of Jenallie’s two other children when they were born.

Jenallie, from Milton Keynes, is believed to have smashed hospital records with the birth.



The biggest baby born in Britain on record is Guy Carr, who weighed 15lbs 8oz at birth in 1992.

Other big babies include George King, who was 15lbs 7oz when he was born in 2013.

And Alpha Stone Mitchell was 14lbs 15oz when he was born in 2021.

News.title: Burnham once wanted Trump banned from Manchester – now comes the toughest test of his statesmanship
News.content:
DONALD Trump was invited to Manchester by Andy Burnham yesterday — despite once vowing to ban the US President from the city.

The new PM spoke to Mr Trump as one of his first actions in a scramble to try and build bridges.



Last month the President branded Mr Burnham “extremely liberal” and the new PM has a long track record of publicly deriding his American counterpart.

In 2021 he blasted: “Any UK politician who gave Trump the time of day should be ashamed.”



And as Manchester Mayor in 2017 he vowed to ban the “deeply troubling” President from the city and called for Trump’s state visit to the UK to be cancelled because of his “extreme views”.

But in their first call yesterday afternoon, Mr Burnham struck a dramatically different tone, congratulating the President on the US-hosted World Cup.



And Mr Trump congratulated the PM on England’s third-place finish.

Ahead of their call Mr Trump hailed Mr Burnham’s yet-to-be-announced plans for expanding North Sea oil extraction, but that could yet fall far short of Mr Trump’s advice to “drill, baby drill”.

No 10 said last night the President had briefed Mr Burnham on the situation in the Middle East.

A spokesman said Mr Burnham stressed the “UK’s commitment to securing the movement of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz to support global supply chains and drive down costs for businesses and families across the country.”



But the appointment of Net Zero devotee Ed Miliband as Foreign Secretary risks flaring tensions due to Mr Trump’s loathing of windmills and his green energy policies.

Sensitive tech and tariff negotiations remain ongoing.

A major flash point also looms over Mr Burnham’s pledge to force US tech firms to pay more in taxes to fund spending.



It will put him on a collision course with the White House, which has vowed to protect their domestic stars like Google, Apple and Meta.

The pair are due to meet at the UN General Assembly in September, with Mr Burnham expected to travel to Miami in December for the G20 summit.

The UK will host it in 2027, with Manchester the likely venue.

News.title: Pupil, 16, who stabbed teacher in the head with kitchen knife is found not guilty of trying to murder her
News.content:
BLADE HORROR Pupil, 16, who stabbed teacher in the head with kitchen knife is found not guilty of trying to murder her

A PUPIL who stabbed his teacher in the head with a kitchen knife has been found not guilty of attempted murder.

The 16-year-old was in an empty classroom with history teacher, Vicki Williams, when he brandished a knife out of his bag and lunged at her.



The court heard the two got into “violent struggle”, with the pupil fleeing the scene after leaving Williams with a wound to her scalp.

A jury found the teen not guilty of attempted murder but guilty of wounding with intent, and unlawful wounding on Monday.



Swansea Crown Court heard that the boy at Milford Haven Comprehensive School in Pembrokeshire, Wales, entered a room and approached Williams’ desk on February 5.

He asked the teacher to check his schoolwork, but Williams said “alarm bells” began to ring in her head when he shut the door to the classroom.

The student, who was 15 at the time, then pulled a kitchen knife out from his bag and struck her in the head.

Williams said she believed she was dying after the incident, which the prosecution said was a “sustained attack” and would have continued had a teacher not intervened and disarmed the boy.

The jury was shown CCTV of the teenager leaving the school premises after the attack and going to his grandmother’s home, telling her: “Something went in my head, nan”.

Williams was rushed to hospital in Haverfordwest and was found to have sustained a wound to her scalp, scratches on her back and minor cuts to her hands.



During the trial, the boy told the court that Williams had tried to “grab” the knife from his rucksack and that he “accidentally assaulted her” in a struggle.

Matthew Roberts KC, defending the teen, suggested the student had taken the kitchen knife into school to “show off” to other boys.

He added: “There was no recorded history of conflict between (the student) and Vicki Williams.

“There is no evidence of any animosity or any ill feeling between them at all.

“(He), we say, had no reason whatsoever to want to hurt Vicki Williams.”



The teenager had previously pleaded guilty to possessing a kitchen knife on the school grounds.

Christopher Rees KC, prosecuting, said in his closing speech last week: “He knows the truth about what he did, he just doesn’t have, I’m afraid, the courage or the remorse to tell anyone about it.

“He brought the knife into school because he planned to attack the teacher.

“Why Vicki Williams? Well, she was, at quarter past three, a lone female teacher, she was an easy target.

“He’s not attacked a male teacher, has he? He’s attacked one of the young female teachers, alone in her classroom.”



The jury reached a majority verdict of 11 to one to convict the boy of wounding with intent after just over four hours of deliberation on Monday.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He will be sentenced on September 3 at Swansea Crown Court.

News.title: Iran ‘counting down the minutes to ground invasion’ as it declares it is in ‘full-scale war’ with US as tensions soar
News.content:
IRAN says it is again in a full-scale war with America and is “counting down the minutes” to the US launching an invasion.

It came after Donald Trump sent more war planes to the region as tensions continue to soar.



The US is deploying extra F-16 and F-35 fighter jets from European bases, as well as more aerial refuelling tankers, in a sign the conflict is about to escalate.

As the now-collapsed peace deal was crumbling last week, US President Trump received a briefing from ­military chiefs on options to intensify the war.



They included capturing Kharg Island, where 90 per cent of Iran’s oil exports pass through, or bombing Iranian nuclear facilities at Pickaxe Mountain.

In a ­further sign the war may become a region-wide ­conflict, Iran’s Yemen-based terror proxy the Houthis have announced a maritime embargo of Saudi Arabia.

The group said it is an “eye for an eye” move after it accused the Saudis of attacks last week.

After trading daily assaults for over a week, Iran and America are again in an all-out war, Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian declared.



He said: “The reality is the Islamic Republic of Iran is engaged in a full-scale war. We must be realistic and accept the natural consequences of this resistance.”

Tehran is talking about facing further American escalation — including a ground invasion.

Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said his nation is counting down the minutes to “welcome” US forces in a ground offensive.



He added that America would face “consequences of any adventure” if it tries to seize Kharg Island.

The US targeted the ­partially built Darkhovin nuclear power plant in the south west of the country in its latest attacks.

It was still under construction, meaning there was no risk of a ­radiation leak.

United States Central Command said it targeted military command centres, air defence sites and missile and drone launch sites.

In response, Iran continued to target ships trying to pass through the Strait of ­Hormuz by the southern route instead of the northern route Tehran demands.



A ship has been ablaze and adrift in the strait after it was attacked. The crew were safely rescued.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guard said two “non-compliant” tankers had been “brought to a halt”.

Despite the escalating attacks, diplomatic exchanges are still taking place between the warring parties.

Messages are being passed via mediators.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mr Trump is said to have not ruled out seeking a diplomatic solution.



US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has insisted the door is still open to a return to the negotiating table.

News.title: Blogger who walked around Moscow naked becomes target of Vladimir Putin’s former ‘lover’ and faces 12 years in prison
News.content:
AN unhinged influencer who strutted naked through Moscow has been slammed as a “depraved trash-blogger” by Putin’s alleged ex-lover.

Anastasia Bragina, 22, claimed that the stunt fulfilled her “soul’s purpose” – but Ekaterina Mizulina, 41, accused her of disseminating porn to children.



Shocking footage shows Bragina, a former reality TV contestant, walking into shops wearing nothing but a thin chain necklace.

She says the scandalous stream now has 21 million views.



The 22-year-old said: “The universe is guiding me along this benevolent, constructive path, taking my soul’s purpose into account, so that I can break free from all limitations.”

But Ekaterina Mizulina, a high-ranking official with Vladimir Putin’s internet watchdog, says she wants to see her locked up for 12 years.



Two years ago there were unconfirmed rumours that Mizulina, 41, and Putin were lovers.

Now, the pro-Kremlin official has slammed Bragina, saying: “The blogger has apparently completely lost her mind and decided to stage a performance in Moscow — she went for a naked walk around the city.

“In that state she walked the streets and entered cafés.

“Everything was of course filmed on video.”



The enraged ex-lover, now married to a pro-Putin singer, has managed to fine the blogger a measly £38 (4,000 rubles).

But police will now begin looking at allegations of “distributing pornography on social media and giving children inappropriate and sexually suggestive advice”, according to Mizulina.

She added: “The trash-blogger is publicly corrupting children on her platforms, constantly appearing naked in video circles, holding conversations in that state with children mainly on intimate subjects, and also giving schoolchildren various pieces of depraved advice.”



But Bragina told her followers: “I realised that deep down I was afraid of appearing naked in front of people in real life, offline.

“I understood, deep within my soul, that this lesson was waiting for me somewhere and that I would have to overcome this limitation.

“So I was lying on the bed when the idea of going to the shop naked simply popped into my head.

“I didn’t feel any particular fear. The thought came to me calmly.”

Mizulina claimed two school children came into her offices to complain about the naked influencer.

News.title: Burnham might be king of the castle now but dethroning has become a deadly hazard in modern politics
News.content:
IF you want a friend in politics, get yourself a dog.

But I hear Andy Burnham is still ­deciding whether to bring his trusty pooch Axel down to London with him.



He might want a familiar face when he discovers just how slippery this bunch of Labour MPs can be.

The very same politicians who slag him off in private now fawn over their new Messiah without shame.



One MP yesterday even had the cheek to wax lyrical about Burnham on the radio, despite referring to him last year as a “mediocre man” who should get back in his Manchester box.

There are enough brass necks in the Parliamentary Labour Party to melt down and build an entire orchestra.



It is not unusual for creatures of Westminster to speak with forked tongues, and journalists like myself are often grateful recipients of MPs unloading in private.

(I know for a fact that some of ­Burnham’s new Cabinet really don’t think he’s all that, having told me as much.)

But the galactic level of brown-nosing has been particularly unedifying in recent weeks as they toady up to their new PM.

“Just horrendous”, is how one minister describes to me the sucking up going on behind closed doors.



I remember when Labour MPs once had the same doe-eyed affection for a certain Keir Rodney Starmer (remember him?)

After being sacked by Burnham yesterday, embittered Steve Reed replied icily: “I hope those who did not show loyalty to Keir will now show it to you.”

Surely the lesson from the last decade of British politics is that there is a fat chance of that.

Not that Burnham needs reminding, having stuck the knife himself into Starmer despite his “nothing to do with me, guv” protests.

His close ally, Louise Haigh, even bizarrely revealed that they had been plotting for a year to bring down Starmer.



The point is that Burnham may feel an unassailable king of the castle right now, but dethroning is an occupational hazard for PMs these days.

Burnham at least has a Praetorian Guard of loyalists around him — a ­“Manchester mafia” — the likes of which Starmer could never rely on.

He also beats the low bar of being a far better communicator, both with the wider country and making time for fragile MPs.



And surely Labour MPs won’t get rid of ANOTHER leader before the next election for risk of looking rather like those ­feckless Tories.

But that does not mean they will roll over and do Burnham’s bidding.

Indeed, they are being given looser leashes as he pledges to rip up the whipping system.

It risks out-of-touch Labour MPs trying to pull even further away from the public’s priorities on the key issues such as welfare and immigration.

The party’s not-so-soft Left think Andy is one of them and will expect him to go on a spending spree to fund all their ­various hobby horses.



Their wishlist will soon come into ­contact with the reality of a Treasury currently spending one in every 12 pounds just paying off our debts.

Burnham’s top appointments are a good omen that he is so far resisting left-wing pressure to stock the Cabinet with hardliners.

In John Healey we have a sensible economic hawk who won’t go crazy with the nation’s credit card, but will plough money into vital areas like his old berth at Defence.

New Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has been kept as far away from the public finances as possible by packing him off abroad.

Although I would love to be a fly on the wall during his first meeting with the Trump administration and its visceral hatred of his Net Zero crusade.



It is smart to keep Shabana Mahmood in the Home Office where she is making genuine strides on migration.

She knows that the public are impatient on small boats and asylum hotels and often finds herself swimming against the tide of her own party.

Starmer’s premiership went south when he gave up trying to govern in the ­interests of the country and instead focused on narrow party interests.



It saw Reform break away in the polls and Labour’s support collapse just two years after that loveless election landslide.

Labour decided that none of those 403 MPs could beat Farage — but thought ­perhaps Burnham just had what it takes.

After returning to Parliament in a by-election, the new PM promised every decision in No10 would be subject to a “Makerfield test”.

What would ordinary folk say about that down the Dog And Duck on a Friday night?

This test will inevitably bring him into friction with some of the MPs who now appear to worship him.



Burnham’s “matey-matey” collaborative approach may need to give way to a ­ruthlessness to drive through his agenda in the interest of mainstream voters.

The former backroom fixer clearly isn’t entirely lily-livered, having embarked on a brutal purge of the Starmerites yesterday.

Sometimes politics is about picking ­battles and it can get lonely at the top.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The last bloke famously said “country first, party second” and then turned it on its head.

Burnham will now have to show his mettle in Downing Street — to stop Britain going to the dogs.

News.title: ‘Beloved’ man, 25, died after medical emergency at popular campsite as three arrested for drug-related offences
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

CAMPSITE TRAGEDY ‘Beloved’ man, 25, died after medical emergency at popular campsite as three arrested for drug-related offences

A “BELOVED” man has died following a medical emergency at a popular campsite – as cops have arrested three.

Officers were called to Penmaenau Farm Camping in Wales at 10.30pm on Saturday, following reports of a medical emergency.



Despite the best efforts of paramedics, Dewi Aeron Evans, 25, was pronounced dead at the scene.

Dyfed-Powys Police arrested three men following the incident on suspicion of drug-related offences at the campsite.



In a heartbreaking tribute, Evans’ family said: “Dewi Aeron Evans, a beloved and dear son, brother and grandson; will be a huge loss to the family and community in Uwchaled.

“The family and community would appreciate privacy at this difficult time.”

Police and paramedics were called to the site on July 18, located next to the Royal Welsh Show.

The event is visited by 200,000 people each year including King Charles and Camilla.

Following the death of Dewi, from Llanfihangel Glyn Myfyr, near Corwen, specially trained officers were deployed to support his next of kin.

Police launched an investigation into the unexplained death, arresting three men in connection with the death.



They have been kept in custody while enquiries continue.

Temporary Chief Superintendent Steve Davies described the death as a “tragic incident”.

He said: “This is a tragic incident, and our thoughts remain with the young man’s family at this difficult time.

“I would like to reassure the public that this is an isolated incident, and the death is currently being treated as unexplained.

“There is no evidence of any ongoing risk to the wider public in connection with this sad incident.”



The Royal Welsh Show said: “We are deeply saddened by this tragic news, and our thoughts are with the young man’s family and friends, and with everyone affected by this incident.

“We will continue to support Dyfed-Powys Police as their enquiries continue.

“The safety and wellbeing of everyone attending the event remains our priority.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We are working closely as members of the Builth Wells Event Safety Group, which has extensive measures in place, including welfare and support services, medical provision and safety initiatives.

“We want everyone attending to feel supported and to have a safe and enjoyable time.”

News.title: Former Miss Universe Jamaica contestant dies suddenly at 35 as tributes pour in
News.content:
Former Miss Universe Jamaica contestant dies suddenly at 35 as tributes pour in

The Miss Universe Jamaica organisation announced the death of the actress and dancer a social media tribute - her cause of death has not been disclosed

View Image LaToya Malcolm has passed away at 35 (Image: LaToya Malcolm/Instagram)

A former Miss Universe Jamaica finalist has passed away at 35.

‌



The Miss Universe Jamaica organisation announced the death of actress and dancer, LaToya Malcolm, on Saturday in a social media tribute.

‌



Her cause of death was not disclosed.

‌



"We are deeply saddened by the passing of Miss Universe Jamaica alumna LaToya Malcolm," the organisation wrote.

It went on to say that she would "never be forgotten."

‌



LaToya competed in the 2024 Miss Universe Jamaica pageant, where she was one of the competition's standout contestants.

She was grieving the loss of her father during the event. LaToya later won the Miss Jamaica Bikini International title and dedicated her win to her dad in a heartfelt message.

Outside of pageantry, LaToya was an an actress and dance instructor.

Article continues below

She was also invested in the Transition Project, a program that helps underprivileged teenagers prepare for adulthood.

Current Miss Universe Jamaica titleholder, Gabrielle Henry, was among those paying tribute. She said LaToya's passing is a "a great loss" whose impact and voice "will not be forgotten."

News.title: Andy Burnham Cabinet picks – live: New PM brings Angela Rayner back into Government
News.content:
New Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, has made sweeping changes to the Cabinet — bringing back Angela Rayner and appointing the experienced John Healey as Chancellor of the Exchequer

Andy Burnham has made his first Cabinet appointments — bringing back Angela Rayner to the fold.

The new Prime Minister has also opted for John Healey as his Chancellor and Ed Miliband as Foreign Secretary. Ms Rayner, who was deputy leader of the Labour Party until she quit amid her stamp duty error, is now the Housing Secretary.

Mr Healey replaces Rachel Reeves in the post with the latter confirming her departure from the Cabinet on social media this afternoon. David Lammy has also gone, vacating the deputy prime minister post, a role to which he was appointed by Keir Starmer last year.

Mr Miliband has been appointed Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs. He takes over from Yvette Cooper as Foreign Secretary in Mr Burnham's Cabinet. Mr Miliband, who also served as leader of the Labour Party from 2010 to 2015, was energy secretary in Mr Starmer's government. Ms Cooper herself is now Health Secretary, a position Wes Streeting held for nearly two years.

Other major figures from the Starmer era have been sacked, including Peter Kyle who was Business Secretary. His replacement is yet to be confirmed. Mr Healey, however, recently resigned as Mr Starmer’s defence secretary in a row over military funding.

But Shabana Mahmood has been reappointed Home Secretary by Mr Burnham. Ms Mahmood, MP for Ladywood, Birmingham, first took on the role in September 2025, replacing Ms Cooper in Mr Starmer's first reshuffle.

Talking today without a lectern or notes, in a huge move away from tradition, Mr Burnham, 56, spoke for 10 minutes and used the opportunity to outline his vision for the UK. He made several vows, stressing his first action will be to set out a plan to end rough sleeping. Minutes after this vow though, his Housing Secretary - Steve Reed OBE - quit.
