Sports.title: Wolff says Russell not alone in Mercedes power woes, was “team mistake” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff claims all Mercedes-powered cars were down on power during the Belgian Grand Prix.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli won the race for Mercedes, but team mate George Russell crashed out on the opening lap after contact with Lewis Hamilton at Les Combes.

Russell later said that while he felt the contact with the Ferrari driver was a racing incident, he implied that a battery deployment problem – which he had been complaining had been affecting his straight-line performance all weekend at Spa-Francorchamps – was more responsible for causing the clash. Wolff accepted that a power unit deployment problem had been a contributing factor.

“I think there’s two situations here,” he told Sky after the race. “First, the racing accident – that happened. Unfortunately, for us, we lost a lot of constructors points and, George, a lot of drivers’ points.

“George tried on the outside, braked late, and that corner should have been his, but it was a racing incident. These things can happen, whether you’re at the front, in the middle, or at the back of the pack. George had a tough weekend. Probably half of that can be attributed to the power unit, which wasn’t as good as it should have been in his car, and the other half perhaps to the driving.

“But we’re in this together. We all make mistakes. Today it was a team mistake on another day it’ll be a driver’s mistake. We just need to minimise those mistakes and support each other.”

Wolff says that Russell was not the only Mercedes-powered driver who was experiencing lower than expected power deployment during the Belgian Grand Prix.

“We had an issue on all Mercedes engines that we lacked the power out on the straights,” he admitted. “That bit him [Russell] badly and it goes one-hundred-percent on us.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We’re trying our best as a team. We have the most powerful power unit – we have a strong car that is capable of winning. Everybody gives their maximum to minimise their mistakes and still it happens – because we are humans at work. We let Kimi down at Silverstone where George got a podium – that was maybe better than the result should have been – one driver DNF’d in Canada, the other DNF’d in Barcelona. That’s a little bit the story of our season, here. It’s a technical sport, it’s a mechanical sport.

“I’m proud to be a part of the organisation at HPP and Mercedes Grand Prix. Those groups of people give it all they have and we came out with a product this year that is so strong and I’d rather fix the reliability than try to accelerate a slow engine or a slow car. We’re giving it one-hundred-percent and we need to give it one-hundred-percent, because we have lost a lot of points through reliability. We should be much further ahead than we are.”

Russell had been slower than than Antonelli throughout the weekend. Wolff suggested that Antonelli may have learned how to maximise the performance from the new-generation power units for 2026 compared to his more experienced team mate.

“I think, first of all, it’s very different and I think this is probably an advantage that Kimi has, because it reset for everyone,” he said.

“Then the components of energy harvesting and energy deployment plays a role. Even the way you go on the throttle – whether you give it full throttle or half throttle and when you lift off – can have consequences in terms of the energy delivery. And that’s another dimension that has been handed to the driving – some drivers may not like it, others may say ‘okay, we just need to get used to it’. But it’s another component that makes it more complex.”

Wolff said he would talk to Russell to console him following his latest setback in the championship, which has seen him drop to third in the standings behind Hamilton.

“I haven’t seen him yet, but it’s completely understandable that the moment you’re out of this race it’s so frustrating and the emotions boil. That’s why I completely understand. He has our one-hundred-percent support. We are trying to solve all the issues, he’s doing everything he can to get on top of his driving. So I haven’t spoken to him, but I’m going to try and put my arms around him.”

Sports.title: Antonelli passes Leclerc to win Belgian GP, Russell out after Hamilton clash | 2026 Belgian Grand Prix report
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the world championship to 45 points after winning the Belgian Grand Prix.

The Mercedes driver had led early on after starting from pole, but a Virtual Safety Car had allowed Charles Leclerc to take the lead in the pit cycle.

Eventually, Antonelli was able to chase down the Ferrari and pass for the lead with 11 laps to go. Max Verstappen completed the podium in third.

At the start, pole winner Antonelli held the lead into La Source, but Verstappen in second managed to get ahead of the Mercedes into Eau Rouge. Verstappen’s time in the lead was shortlived, however, as Antonelli passed the Red Bull back down the Kemmel Straight, with Leclerc also following through into second place.

Behind, a three-way fight for fourth between George Russell, Lewis Hamilton and Oscar Piastri ended in tears when Russell and Hamilton collided through Les Combes, sending the Mercedes spinning into the gravel trap and out of the race. Hamilton was able to continue, but was later handed a five second time penalty for being deemed responsible for the collision.

After a Safety Car to recover Russell’s car, the race resumed on lap five with Antonelli leading from Leclerc and Verstappen. Antonelli headed the field until a brief Virtual Safety Car on lap 18 to clear debris, which turned green by the time Antonelli had pitted for Hard tyres.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Leclerc remained out a handful more laps than Antonelli, until a second debris-related VSC was triggered on lap 20. This allowed Ferrari to pit both Leclerc and Hamilton, to serve his penalty, and enabled Leclerc to rejoin the circuit still under VSC ahead of Antonelli, taking what was effectively the lead of the race.

After Lando Norris pitted, Leclerc took the overall race lead, but Antonelli began to slowly reel him in. Eventually, on lap 34, Antonelli tucked up behind the Ferrari along the Kemmel Straight and overtook Leclerc to take the lead.

While Leclerc tried his best to remain in touch with with the championship leader, Antonelli was able to keep ahead of the Ferrari until the chequered flag, heading him by just under two seconds. Verstappen was around ten seconds behind the pair in third, with Hamilton taking fourth place after passing Piastri in the later laps.

Isack Hadjar moved from 21st on the grid to finish sixth, ahead of Lando Norris, Gabriel Bortoleto and Arvid Lindblad. Franco Colapinto took the final point in tenth for Alpine, ahead of team mate Pierre Gasly.

Hamilton will be investigated after the race for an unsafe pit release after one of the Ferrari mechanics was struck by his right-front wheel as he was released from his pit stop. Ferrari confirmed to Hamilton over team radio that the mechanic involved was unhurt.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Tests Boxing’s No-Promoter Model With DAZN Deal
Sports.content:
Promoters normally negotiate purses, secure venues, organize undercards, market events and absorb much of the financial risk involved in staging a card. Those jobs do not disappear because a fighter signs directly with a broadcaster. DAZN has not explained how those responsibilities will be divided, leaving open the possibility that outside promoters or event partners will handle different aspects of each show.

The signing also gives Teofimo more control over his career. Rather than being tied to one promotional company, he has greater freedom to negotiate fights while DAZN continues expanding beyond its role as a broadcaster. After strengthening its relationship with Premier Boxing Champions and adding more high-profile talent, the company is moving toward direct deals with elite fighters instead of relying entirely on promoters to deliver events.

The signing is also a gamble. Teofimo remains one of boxing’s biggest personalities, but he is coming off a disappointing loss to Shakur Stevenson that damaged his standing among the sport’s top names. His first fight after the announcement is another difficult assignment when he challenges WBA welterweight champion Rolando ‘Rolly’ Romero on August 22 in Las Vegas.

A victory would immediately strengthen DAZN’s investment. Another loss would leave Teofimo with consecutive defeats and force the company to sell one of its newest signings coming off back-to-back setbacks.

DAZN deserves credit for trying something different. If direct fighter deals become common, the balance of power in boxing could shift away from exclusive promotional contracts. The risk is that DAZN may have made its move at the wrong moment. Teofimo still has name recognition and drawing power, but those advantages shrink quickly if the wins stop coming. That’s what makes this signing one of the more interesting business bets in boxing this year.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Wants Gary Antuanne Russell If Haney Fight Fails
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson still wants Devin Haney for his October Zuffa Boxing debut, but he already has another name in mind if that fight doesn’t happen. Stevenson identified Gary Antuanne Russell this week as the opponent he would pursue instead, calling him one of the toughest fighters he has ever shared the ring with. Russell holds the WBA light welterweight title.

“I would like maybe like a Antuanne, Gary Antuanne. There are fighters out there that are real good fighters, so it’s like you can’t say there’s nobody to fight. Antoine is a hell of a fighter,” said Shakur to Fighthype about who he wants to fight in October if he can’t get Haney. “Antuanne, I think me and Antuanne should be a big fight. I know he was talking about getting the belts before, but if you didn’t start the process of getting the belts, then me and you probably could get in there and rumble right now. It ain’t really no point of waiting.”

Shakur then explained why Russell sits near the top of his list of potential opponents.

Sports.title: Dalton Smith’s First Title Defense May Be Tougher Than Winning The Belt
Sports.content:
Winning a world title is one thing. Keeping it is often much harder. Mandatory challengers usually spend months studying the champion’s strengths and weaknesses, and they enter the fight with everything on the line. Puello fits that description.

Although many fans remember him for losing his title to Subriel Matias, the Dominican southpaw remains one of the most awkward fighters in the division. His movement, defensive style and left-handed stance present different problems than the pressure Smith handled when he stopped Matias to win the belt. Smith knows he isn’t overlooking the assignment.

“Becoming World Champion was something I’d dreamed about my whole life, but winning the belt was never the end goal. I want to build a legacy, and that starts with defending the title against the best challengers in the division,” said Dalton. “Puello has been a World Champion before and earned his mandatory position, so I know exactly how tough this fight will be. I’ll be giving him the respect he deserves in training, but once that first bell goes, it’ll be about showing why I’m the WBC World Champion.”

The postponement may have worked in Puello’s favor. Instead of meeting Smith in May, the former champion received several extra months to prepare while Smith recovered. Additional preparation time rarely hurts an experienced challenger, particularly one who has already won a world title.

Smith will still deserve to be the favorite fighting in front of his hometown crowd, but homecoming fights bring their own pressure. Sheffield fans will expect another impressive performance after his title-winning knockout of Matias, while Puello arrives with nothing to lose.

If Smith defeats Puello, attention will shift to unification fights and the division’s biggest names. If he underestimates an experienced former champion, those plans could disappear before they ever get started.

Sports.title: Keyshawn Fight Gives Haney More Leverage Than Shakur
Sports.content:
The purse bid also creates an awkward situation for Shakur. He has publicly welcomed a Haney-Keyshawn fight, but a Haney defeat may actually work against him. Shakur and Keyshawn have repeatedly referred to each other as brothers, making a fight between them look highly unlikely. If Keyshawn wins the title, one of Shakur’s biggest available opponents disappears.

A Devin victory leaves the door open for Shakur. Haney would remain champion, the fight would still carry championship stakes, and both fighters would have another reason to keep talking. Haney would also have little reason to accept a 144-pound handicap after successfully defending his title.

If Haney vacates instead, there is still no guarantee that the Shakur fight gets made. Ryan Garcia is tied up with Conor Benn, and Benn has already rejected the idea of accepting terms that favor Shakur. Ryan also has little reason to agree to another weight restriction after the disadvantage he dealt with against Gervonta Davis.

The purse bid puts Haney on the clock, but it also exposes a flaw in Shakur’s position. Haney has far more leverage by defending his title against Keyshawn than by surrendering it in hopes of landing a fight that has not been agreed to. If Shakur wants one of the biggest fights available, keeping Haney as a champion serves his interests far better than watching Keyshawn take the belt, who he refers to as his ‘brother’ and will never fight.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker Gets IBF Eliminator Against Conor Wallace on October 3
Sports.content:
While Wallace holds the higher ranking, his record has been built almost entirely against regional-level opposition in Australia. The 30-year-old has yet to beat an established world contender despite spending eight years in the professional ranks. His biggest victories have come against fighters such as Jerome Pampellone and Dylan Colin, making it difficult to judge how he will perform against the most talented opponent of his career.

Whittaker has also been criticized for the level of his opposition as a professional, but he brings a much stronger amateur background into the eliminator. The Olympic silver medalist defeated several elite amateurs during his run to the 2020 Olympic final before losing to Cuba’s Arlen López in the gold medal bout. That experience against elite international competition gives him an advantage that Wallace does not possess.

If Bivol keeps hold of the IBF title, the winner will move into position for a championship fight under the sanctioning body’s rules.

This is a fight for Whittaker, 29, that should provide a clearer picture of his true standing among the global elite. Wallace’s ranking makes him a legitimate opponent, but his record leaves questions about how much resistance he can offer against a fighter with Whittaker’s amateur pedigree.

Sports.title: Barry Hearn Sees Different Anthony Joshua Before Prenga Fight
Sports.content:
“AJ is in an amazing place at the moment. Obviously, I’ve seen him since 2012. We’ve got very close. He’s like a member of our family. “I don’t think I’ve seen him so motivated for the long term. Some of that’s been fueled by that tragic accident, but he’s now talking about the next three years in the ring. It was a year ago that we were talking about potentially two fights and then go off to a happy retirement. “He’s very motivated; he feels good about himself, but boxing is a funny sport. It takes one punch from a big lad to knock out anyone in the world. So, you’ve got to be on your toes all the time. You can’t take this for granted. And when you get your chance, you’ve got to take it. “AJ is in the mood to cause a lot of pain on Saturday. I don’t think I’ve seen him look better than this in the 14 years I’ve known him. He is in the right place, and I think on Saturday in Jeddah will be the right time,” Barry Hearn told Sky Sports.

Prenga wasn’t chosen to be a threat. He’s there to give Joshua rounds after the accident. Gym performances don’t mean much when the opponent isn’t expected to test you. Until Joshua gets back in with a heavyweight who can crack and force him to answer questions, nobody knows if the flaws from the Dubois fight remain. Barry Hearn’s comments are what you’d expect from a promoter backing one of his biggest stars.

Joshua was stopped by Daniel Dubois in 2024. AJ rebounded from that defeat last December, knocking out the YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul in a fight that was largely viewed as a celebrity-esque spectacle. Even in that victory, Joshua looked vulnerable before knocking out Paul.

AJ has always looked like a million bucks on the scale or hitting pads in the gym, but that means very little once someone real lands a clean shot on his chin.

He can look as motivated as Barry Hearn says, but gym work can’t replicate how a fighter reacts to getting hit, especially after coming back from a car accident. If Prenga manages to land something solid on Saturday, we’ll see right away if those old vulnerabilities are still there.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn: Boots Ennis Is ‘King Of The Castle’
Sports.content:
The way Hearn sees it, Vergil Jr. has nothing that Boots wants other than the money the fight would bring in. He doesn’t hold a major belt. The WBC interim 154-lb title isn’t enough.

Hearn says his fighter is no longer in the position of making concessions to land the bout. Boots is now “king of the castle.”

“He was taking the smaller side of the piece last time. He was going to be the B-side. He agreed to everything that they wanted to get that opportunity. So you imagine how he feels now that he’s king of the castle,” said Hearn to the media about Ennis’ position in negotiations with Vergil Ortiz Jr. “Vergil doesn’t have anything Boots wants other than a big fight and a big payday. What does Boots want to do now? He wants to unify.” “I don’t rule out that Ortiz fight at all. One thing is for sure. He ain’t close at all at the moment.“

Hearn’s comments reflect how much Ennis’ position has changed over the past year. During earlier discussions, Ennis was still chasing the biggest opportunities and was willing to accept B-side status to secure a fight with Ortiz. Hearn says those circumstances no longer exist.

Ennis now holds two world titles and has shifted his attention toward becoming the undisputed champion. Hearn indicated that unification bouts remain the priority, but he left the door open for Ortiz if Golden Boy presents an offer that outweighs Ennis’ other options.

“Tell us what the money is. And I’ll go to Jaron, and I’ll say, ‘We got Kelly, Fundora, or Ortiz,'” said Hearn.

Unless Turki Alalshikh gets involved, it’s questionable if a fight with Ortiz Jr. is financially appealing enough for Ennis to take time off from pursuing his goal of becoming the undisputed champion at junior middleweight.

Sports.title: Vernon Forrest Outboxes Shane Mosley Again in 2002 Rematch
Sports.content:
Six months after defeating Mosley to capture the championship, Forrest again relied on his size, jab and disciplined boxing to earn a 12-round unanimous decision and settle the rivalry once and for all.

The rematch carried enormous significance. Forrest defended both the WBC and Ring Magazine welterweight championships after taking them from Mosley in their first meeting earlier in the year in January 2002. Many believed Mosley would make the necessary adjustments and reclaim the titles, while Forrest had the opportunity to prove the upset had not been a one-night performance.

The event attracted 15,775 fans, the largest crowd to attend a boxing card in Indiana history at the time. HBO televised the championship bout nationally, and both fighters earned career-high paydays. Forrest received $3.42 million, while Mosley collected $2.8 million. Veteran referee Laurence Cole officiated the 12-round title fight.

Mosley came out aggressively, looking to erase the disappointment of the first bout by forcing exchanges from the opening bell. Forrest refused to be drawn into a firefight. Standing three inches taller with the longer reach, he established his jab early, circled effectively and answered Mosley’s rushes with sharp counters before tying him up whenever the action moved inside.

As the rounds progressed, Forrest steadily took control. Forrest repeatedly stabbed Mosley with the jab before tying him up whenever the challenger got close, forcing Mosley to reset his offense over and over. Referee Laurence Cole was forced to separate the fighters throughout the contest as the tactical battle became increasingly physical.

The middle rounds lacked sustained action, drawing boos from portions of the crowd, but Forrest remained committed to the game plan. One report even noted that a fight in the stands during the sixth round briefly attracted as much attention as the action inside the ring.

Mosley increased the pressure during the championship rounds, finally producing several spirited exchanges in the tenth. Forrest answered with crisp counterpunching and finished strongly, landing several hard right hands late in the eleventh before boxing confidently through the final round. There were no knockdowns, but Forrest consistently landed the cleaner, more effective punches.

CompuBox statistics reflected the tactical nature of the contest. Forrest landed 120 of 446 punches, while Mosley connected on 114 of 259, with Forrest’s jab, timing and ring control outweighing Mosley’s higher connect percentage.

Judges Gary Merritt (117-111), Tony Castellano (116-112) and Jerry Roth (115-113) all favored Forrest. HBO unofficial scorer Harold Lederman and several media scorecards also had Forrest winning, confirming that his first victory had been no accident.

The rematch closed the book on one of the era’s most compelling rivalries. Forrest had defeated Mosley twice as a professional after also beating him during the 1992 U.S. Olympic Trials, establishing a rare mastery over one of boxing’s greatest fighters.

Mosley later captured world titles in higher weight classes, while Forrest continued his championship run before unifying the welterweight division. More than two decades later, the rematch remains one of the signature victories of Forrest’s Hall of Fame career, removing any doubt that his success against Mosley was built on superior technique rather than surprise.

Ghana News.title: Forms Capital & MobileMoney Fintech rebrand ‘XtraBalance’ as ‘MoMo Boost’ to drive customer adoption
Ghana News.content:
Forms Capital Limited, in partnership with MobileMoney Fintech Limited, has officially rebranded its mobile money overdraft service, 'XtraBalance', as 'MoMo Boost', in a move aimed at improving customer understanding, strengthening brand recognition, and driving wider adoption among MTN MoMo users.



The company said the rebranding is designed to make the service easier to identify and better communicate its purpose, while maintaining the same features and benefits customers already enjoy.



Although the name has changed, the service remains unchanged. MoMo Boost continues to provide eligible MTN MoMo customers with instant access to an overdraft facility that enables them to complete transactions even when their mobile money wallet balance is insufficient.



According to the company, the new name more accurately reflects the value the service provides by giving customers a financial boost whenever they need it most.



Speaking on the rebranding, the head of business development at Forms Capital Limited, Ishmael Abbey, said the decision was informed by customer feedback and the company's commitment to making its products more accessible.



"At Forms Capital, we are constantly listening to our customers and improving our products to meet their needs. The transition from XtraBalance to MoMo Boost is more than a name change; it is about making our service simpler to understand and easier to remember. Customers can continue to enjoy the same reliable overdraft service that helps them complete important transactions even when their wallet balance falls short. Our goal is to remove confusion and ensure more Ghanaians confidently take advantage of this innovative financial solution," he said.



How MoMo Boost Works



MoMo Boost is an overdraft service available to eligible MTN MoMo customers. It automatically covers the shortfall whenever there is not enough money in a customer's mobile money wallet to complete an eligible transaction.



Rather than having a transaction declined because of insufficient funds, the service enables payments or transfers to proceed seamlessly by providing the required top-up amount.



Eligible customers who successfully register for the service are assigned a credit line ranging from GHS 50 to GHS 5,000, depending on their usage and repayment history.



The overdraft is automatically applied whenever a customer initiates an eligible transaction through the MTN MoMo USSD platform or the MTN MoMo app and the available wallet balance is insufficient.



Customers are charged interest only on the amount they use and not on their total approved credit limit.



Repayment is automated. Whenever funds are received into the customer's mobile money wallet through cash deposits or other qualifying credits, the outstanding MoMo Boost amount is recovered automatically without requiring any additional action from the customer.



The service supports a wide range of mobile money transactions, including money transfers, cash withdrawals, merchant and business payments, utility bill payments, airtime and data purchases, government and tax payments, and other eligible MTN MoMo wallet transactions.



Existing Customers Automatically Migrated



Forms Capital assured existing XtraBalance users that they do not need to register again. Their credit limits, transaction history, and repayment arrangements remain unchanged.



According to the company, the only difference customers will notice is the new name.



The company is encouraging eligible MTN MoMo customers who have not yet activated the service to register and enjoy uninterrupted access to funds whenever their wallet balance falls short.



Forms Capital also emphasised that the rebranding does not affect the safety, reliability, or operational features of the service.



The company said it remains committed to delivering innovative digital financial solutions that promote financial inclusion, improve convenience, and expand access to responsible credit for individuals and small businesses across Ghana.



Forms Capital Limited is a regulated specialized deposit-taking institution with more than a decade of experience providing financial solutions to individuals and small and medium-sized enterprises.

Through its digital lending products, XtraCash and MoMo Boost, and its partnership with MTN Ghana on the MTN MoMo platform, the company has expanded access to instant credit for thousands of Ghanaians, particularly underserved individuals and microbusinesses.

Ghana News.title: Mahama confident of peaceful Dagbon succession after Ya-Na’s passing
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has expressed confidence that the succession process in the Dagbon Kingdom will proceed peacefully following the death of the Overlord of Dagbon, His Royal Majesty Ya-Na Abukari Mahama II, saying the late monarch left behind strong institutions to safeguard stability.

The President gave the assurance when a delegation from the Dagbon Traditional Council and the Northern Regional House of Chiefs paid a courtesy call on him at the Presidency to formally notify him of the passing of the Ya-Na, who died on July 16.

Offering condolences to the chiefs and people of Dagbon, President Mahama said the late king's reign would be remembered for strengthening peace and laying a solid institutional framework to ensure continuity in the traditional governance of the kingdom.

He said one of the most significant achievements of the late Ya-Na was his leadership in securing the unanimous adoption of the Dagbon Constitution, which has provided a clear framework for governance, succession and the preservation of peace.

According to the president, the constitutional reforms championed by the late monarch would help guarantee an orderly transition and sustain the gains made in restoring unity to Dagbon.

"I'm positive that he has laid the foundation for a smooth succession in Dagbon. And I wish to assure the chiefs and people of Dagbon that government is standing in full solidarity with you during this period of mourning. We shall work closely with the Dagbon Traditional Council to ensure that the appropriate state courtesies and support are extended as preparations are made for the final funeral rites of our departed king," he said.

President Mahama described Ya-Na Abukari Mahama II as a unifying leader whose patience, humility and commitment to reconciliation helped transform Dagbon into a symbol of peace after years of division.

He said the late Overlord recognised that lasting peace could only be sustained through strong and credible institutions rather than individual leadership, a vision that guided his efforts to strengthen the kingdom's governance structures.

The President further assured the traditional authorities that the government would continue to collaborate closely with the Dagbon Traditional Council throughout the mourning period to ensure that the late monarch received befitting state courtesies and support during the funeral arrangements.

The passing of Ya-Na Abukari Mahama II marks the end of a reign widely credited with consolidating peace and promoting reconciliation in Dagbon following years of conflict, with traditional leaders expected to commence the customary processes leading to the selection of a successor in accordance with Dagbon tradition and the kingdom's constitutional framework.

Ghana News.title: Wontumi’s 20-year sentence serves justice to communities devastated by galamsey – Tanko Computer
Ghana News.content:
Deputy Director of IT and Elections of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Rashid Tanko Computer, says the sentence handed to New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, represents justice for communities that have suffered the devastating effects of illegal mining.

Speaking on JoyNews' The Pulse, Mr Tanko Computer said the conviction goes beyond the punishment of an individual, arguing that it is also about addressing the destruction caused to Ghana's environment and the lives of people living in mining-affected communities.

He said the consequences of illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, have been severe, with polluted water bodies, destroyed forests and serious health concerns affecting residents.

"Justice has been served to the good people of the environment, which has been destroyed, and those children who are now suffering from birth defects. Kidneys have now been destroyed because of the activities of Akonta Mining and its affiliates," he said.

Mr Tanko Computer criticised discussions that focus solely on whether a 20-year sentence is excessive, arguing that attention should also be given to the impact of illegal mining on communities.

According to him, many victims of environmental destruction have suffered silently while individuals involved in illegal mining pursued personal wealth.

He explained that Ghana's laws provide for sentences ranging from 15 to 25 years for such offences and suggested that, considering the extent of the alleged damage, the maximum sentence would have been appropriate.

"In fact, I was expecting about 25. He should have taken the 25. The judge was lenient to have given him the 20 years," he said.

Mr Tanko Computer added that the conviction should serve as a warning to others involved in illegal mining that political influence or personal connections cannot shield them from accountability.

"This will serve as a deterrent to others who think that they can get away with this just because of your own parochial interest," he said.

He stressed that the state's responsibility is to protect citizens and ensure that individuals whose actions threaten public health, livelihoods and natural resources are punished.

His comments follow the Accra High Court's conviction and sentencing of Chairman Wontumi to 20 years' imprisonment over illegal mining activities on the Samreboi concession in the Western Region.

Ghana News.title: Two vehicles destroyed in Mahean fire, school bus damaged
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) has confirmed that two vehicles were destroyed while a school bus sustained partial damage in a fire outbreak at Mahean near Divine Glory School in the Greater Accra Region on Monday night.

According to the GNFS, personnel from the Anyaa Fire Station responded promptly after the Fire Master Control received a distress call at 9:40 p.m.

The firefighting crew, led by ADO II Tetteh David Quansah, was dispatched a minute later and arrived at the scene at 10:02 p.m. The fire was brought under control by 10:18 p.m. and completely extinguished at 10:54 p.m.

The fire completely destroyed a Toyota Highlander with registration number GN-3868-Y and a Nissan Sentra with registration number GE-6765-12.

A Nissan Coaster school bus with registration number GT-2061-N sustained partial fire damage. Firefighters prevented the blaze from spreading to nearby properties and other vehicles.

The GNFS said no casualties were recorded in the incident. It added that investigations are underway to establish the cause of the fire.

Ghana News.title: GMet presents Ghana Climate Atlas to NDPC to strengthen climate-informed development planning
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet) has presented the Ghana Climate Atlas to the National Development Planning Commission (NDPC) as part of efforts to integrate climate information into Ghana's national development planning and policymaking processes.

The presentation followed GMet's request for a strategic partnership with the Commission to demonstrate how the Atlas can support policy formulation, public investment decisions, climate risk management and long-term development planning.

Speaking during the engagement, Principal Meteorologist Ms Maureen Abla Ahiataku said the Atlas, developed with support from the Government of Denmark through the Danish Meteorological Institute, is Ghana's first comprehensive long-term climate projection platform.

Officially launched in March 2026, it provides historical climate data and future projections at the national, regional, district and agro-ecological levels.

Ms Ahiataku explained that the platform, although developed with international support, is managed by GMet staff to ensure its long-term sustainability.

She said the Atlas provides projections on rainfall, temperature and sea-level rise under different greenhouse gas emission scenarios, allowing users to assess climate conditions up to the end of the century.

Under a medium-emission scenario, Ghana's average temperature is projected to increase from about 27.8°C to around 29°C by 2081, while coastal communities are expected to remain vulnerable to sea-level rise, erosion and other climate-related threats.

She also disclosed that GMet is expanding its public weather alert systems through WhatsApp notifications, the Common Alerting Protocol and planned location-specific alerts via telecommunications networks.

Responding on behalf of the NDPC, Director-General Dr Audrey Smock Amoah described the presentation as timely, saying climate information would be critical to the preparation and implementation of Ghana's long-term national development plan.

She urged GMet to align key climate indicators with the Commission's forthcoming national results framework and Sustainable Development Goals reporting system, adding that closer collaboration would help mainstream the Ghana Climate Atlas into national and sub-national planning while strengthening climate-resilient development across the country.

Ghana News.title: Court’s judgment against Wontumi was fair and sound – Martin Kpebu
Ghana News.content:
Private legal practitioner Martin Kpebu has defended the conviction of New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, describing the judgment as fair, well-reasoned and firmly grounded in the evidence presented during the trial.

Speaking on Joy FM's Top Story, Mr Kpebu said he was present in court for a substantial portion of the delivery of the judgment and was satisfied with the judge's analysis of the case.

"The judgment is very fair. Very fair. I was in court—not throughout the whole judgment—but I listened to at least more than half of it. The judge was very sound," he said on Monday, July 20.

According to him, the conviction was not unexpected because the prosecution's case was supported by direct testimony from a key witness who admitted carrying out the illegal mining activities.

Mr Kpebu explained that the second prosecution witness testified that Chairman Wontumi had given him access to the concession where the illegal mining took place.

"The person who was given the opportunity to do the galamsey came to testify as the second prosecution witness. He did the galamsey and testified that Chairman Wontumi gave him the land to mine," he stated.

He argued that because the mining operations were not lawfully authorised, the evidence pointed to illegal mining and significantly strengthened the prosecution's case.

"Once the gentleman who did the actual mining operations is testifying against Wontumi, and once there is no evidence to discredit him as a liar or show he had ulterior motives, Wontumi was bound to be convicted," Mr Kpebu said.

The private legal practitioner described the case as "an open and shut case," adding that the conviction was the natural outcome of the evidence presented before the court.

"This day was always coming," he remarked.

Mr Kpebu's comments come after the Accra High Court sentenced Chairman Wontumi to 20 years' imprisonment over illegal mining activities on the Samreboi concession in the Western Region.

However, the NPP, at a press conference after the conviction, described the judgement as a "travesty of justice" and vowed to appeal the judgement.

Ghana News.title: NPA rejects claims of financial loss in Auditor-General’s report
Ghana News.content:
The National Petroleum Authority (NPA) has dismissed media reports suggesting that the Auditor-General’s recent Performance Audit Report uncovered financial losses, corruption or misappropriation within the Authority, insisting that such claims do not reflect the contents of the audit.

In a statement issued on Monday, July 20, the NPA said the Auditor-General’s Performance Audit Report on its operations covering the period from 2023 to 2025 did not establish any financial loss or revenue loss to the Authority.

It stressed that media characterisations describing the report as evidence of “rot”, corruption or financial impropriety were not findings contained in the audit.

The Authority also criticised a publication by The NewsCenta newspaper, stating that the report failed to include management’s responses to the Auditor-General’s findings. According to the NPA, omitting its official response presented an incomplete picture of the audit outcomes.

Reaffirming its commitment to transparency, accountability and sound corporate governance, the Authority said it would continue to work constructively with the Ghana Audit Service.

It added that it would implement appropriate recommendations from the audit to strengthen regulatory oversight, improve operational efficiency and enhance consumer protection in Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector.

The NPA further urged the public to rely only on its official communications regarding the matter, assuring stakeholders of its continued commitment to maintaining high standards of governance and effective regulation within the petroleum industry.

Ghana News.title: Meet the 3 Ghanaian founders teaching AI to follow the preacher
Ghana News.content:
Founders from left to right (Emmanuel Zeye-CIO, Charles Opoku-Agyeman -CTO, Tony Marfo-CEO)

Every Sunday morning, long before the first note of worship plays, a small army is already at work behind the scenes. Someone is queuing up the slides.

Someone else is testing microphones and checking the livestream feed. A media volunteer is scrambling to find the right Bible verse the moment the pastor references it, while another is already thinking about how Sunday's message will reach people who couldn't make it in.

It's a scene that repeats itself in thousands of churches every week — and it's exactly the problem three Ghanaian entrepreneurs set out to solve.

Their answer isn't a flashy new worship app or another livestreaming tool. It's artificial intelligence, applied quietly and practically to the parts of church life that eat up the most time and the most volunteers.

An Idea Born From Watching, Not Planning

The founders, Tony Marfo, Charles Opoku-Agyeman and Emmanuel Zeye, didn't start with a business plan. They started by paying attention.

Across churches of every size and denomination, they kept seeing the same friction points: media teams struggling to keep pace with pastors mid-sermon, powerful teachings that took hours to prepare but were heard once and then filed away, and congregations that wanted deeper engagement during the week but didn't have the staff or time to make it happen.

Instead of treating those gaps as just part of church life, the team built two platforms to close them.

Two Tools, One Job: Helping Churches Show Up Better

ScriptureLive handles the live moment. As a pastor preaches, it listens for scripture references and pulls up the right verse on screen – for the room and for the livestream — in real time. It also manages worship lyrics, presentation themes and the broader media workflow churches juggle every Sunday.

PostSermon picks up where the service ends. Rather than letting a sermon disappear into a video archive after one viewing, it turns that message into blog posts, devotionals, newsletters, podcast episodes, Bible study guides and social content automatically.

A single sermon can now reach people all week long, across the channels they actually use.

Between the two, the founders say they're covering a church's full cycle: before the sermon, during it, and long after the doors close.

Technology in Service of Ministry, Not in Place of It

The founders are clear about where they draw the line. AI can queue a slide or draft a devotional, but it can't sit with a grieving family, disciple a new believer, or lead a congregation in prayer. Those remain — and will stay — deeply human responsibilities.

What AI can do is take the repetitive, administrative weight off ministry teams, freeing them to spend more of their time on people instead of logistics. That principle has guided every feature the team has built.



Built in Ghana, Designed for the World

Most AI headlines still trace back to Silicon Valley. This team is betting that doesn't have to be the rule.

They're building from Accra with churches in Nairobi, London, Toronto, Sydney and São Paulo in mind — a reminder that fintech isn't the only sector where African startups can compete on a global stage. Faith tech, they believe, is next.

A Market That's Only Getting Bigger

Church life has moved well beyond the four walls of a sanctuary. Livestreams, social media, podcasts and apps are now standard parts of how congregations connect during the week, not just on Sundays.

As that shift continues, so does the demand for tools that make it easier for churches to communicate, engage and extend their reach — which is exactly the gap this Ghanaian team is betting its future on.

What's Next

The founders describe their work as part of something bigger than two products: a push to help churches use technology in ways that strengthen their mission rather than dilute it. As more ministries go digital, Ghana is emerging as an unlikely but credible source of that innovation.

Church leaders, denominational teams, technology partners and investors interested in the future of faith-based technology can connect with the founders directly:

ScriptureLive — scripturelive.app

PostSermon — postsermon.com

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
