A planned metro system in Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, has moved a step closer after the authorities launched a 188 million zloty (€43 million) tender for “pre-design” of the project. City authorities say the plans – which will include a feasibility study, environmental report, geological research, and assessment of the project’s impact on existing buildings – are a major milestone in the development of what would be only Poland’s second underground railway network. #Krakow #metro #projektowanie #przetargi 🚇Kraków ogłasza przetarg na opracowanie dokumentacji przedprojektowej dla budowy metra. W ramach uruchomionego postępowania powstaną m. in. dokumenty, analizy i decyzje, które pozwolą przygotować dokumentację niezbędną do finalnego… pic.twitter.com/0jcYL4HGRq — Kraków (@krakow_pl) July 13, 2026 The idea of building a metro in Kraków has been discussed for decades and, in 2014, 55% of residents who took part in a referendum voted in favour of the project. However, only in 2024 did the city’s then-mayor, Aleksander Miszalski, announce plans to build a system. In September last year, the city unveiled the metro’s planned route, with two lines travelling through the city’s historic centre from its southwestern and southeastern suburbs to its eastern outskirts. In May this year, Miszalski, who had made developing the metro part of his election campaign in 2023, was removed as mayor in a recall referendum. But the project has nevertheless continued, with the municipal authorities last week announcing a tender for pre-design of the metro. The work will include confirmation of the planned structure of the system as well as the location of stations, tunnels and other infrastructure. The city has allocated 188 million zloty for the pre-design in its budget for 2026 to 2031. Studies of feasibility and impact are particularly important given that the planned route of the metro envisages it skirting around Kraków’s Old Town, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site that contains many historical structures. The tender follows months of preparatory work, initial market consultations, analyses and discussions with experts, said Maria Wojtacha, director of Kraków’s public works department. “Although this process doesn’t yet mean that construction has begun, it is one of the most important steps that the city can take individually,” Wojtacha added. “Our goal is to prepare Kraków for the next stage – the ‘design and build’ phase.” The experiences of other recent major infrastructure projects in Poland, such as a major new airport and transport hub and Warsaw’s second metro line, show that environmental and tender procedures need not slow investments down, said Marek Grochowicz of the city’s strategy and European funds department. However, it is clear that the earlier timeline for Kraków’s metro outlined is slipping. Last September, the city said that it hoped construction would begin in 2030 and that the system would be finished by 2035. However, the current acting mayor, Stanisław Kracik, announced last month that construction is unlikely to start until between 2040 and 2045. Even the current tender for “pre-design” work envisages a timeline of up to 50 months for that work alone. Warsaw has announced 56m zloty for “pre-design” work on a fourth metro line. The mayor says improving public transport is an "absolute priority". But his rival in next month's elections says the mayor is digging up forgotten plans as part of the campaign https://t.co/lg3zkNeW2E — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 15, 2024 Rafał Solecki, head of Kraków’s department of strategy and European funds, also made clear last week that “construction of the metro exceeds the financial capabilities of the local authorities”, and that therefore financial support from the national government and the EU will be necessary. “The metro should be treated as a national strategic investment, similar to large railway, road, aviation and metropolitan projects implemented in other parts of the country with state participation,” he added. The city also announced that it has received a proposal for a consortium of seven local universities and research institutions to provide scientific and expert support for the metro project throughout its preparation and implementation. “Building a metro in a historic city is an extremely complex undertaking, requiring special attention to the protection of cultural heritage,” said Andrzej Szarata, rector of Cracow University of Technology. “Therefore, the support of the scientific community…is of paramount importance.” Kraków has been named Europe's best city break destination by members of @WhichUK. Poland says that the number of attempted illegal crossings by migrants over the border from Belarus fell from around 15,500 in the first half of last year to less than 250 in the same period this year – a drop of over 98%. It also now claims to have a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who manage to cross illegally. “The effectiveness of [border guard] officers and the Polish armed forces discourages migrants from taking risks,” says Poland’s interior ministry. Bezpieczeństwo na granicy z Białorusią w pierwszej połowie 2026 r. w liczbach: 📉 Ponad 65-krotny spadek prób nielegalnego przekroczenia (ok. 235 vs ponad 15,5 tys. w pierwszym półroczu 2025 r.) 🛡️ 0 udanych prób nielegalnego przekroczenia granicy 💯 Skuteczność ochrony: 100%… pic.twitter.com/1lTXV56JdW — MSWiA 🇵🇱 (@MSWiA_GOV_PL) July 18, 2026 Since 2021, large numbers of migrants and asylum seekers – mainly from Africa and Asia – have tried to irregularly cross the border from Belarus to Poland with the help and encouragement of the Belarusian authorities. In 2021 alone, just under 40,000 attempted illegal crossings were recorded. While Poland subsequently strengthened border infrastructure and sent thousands of additional officers to bolster security, attempted crossings remained high: there were just under 30,000 in each of 2024 and 2025. However, those figures have now fallen dramatically in the first half of this year, when Poland’s border guard recorded only 235 crossings, compared to 15,500 in the equivalent period for 2025. Meanwhile, the interior minister says that the number of successful crossings by migrants – i.e. those who managed to get across the border and were not apprehended – has fallen to zero so far this year, down from around 1,700 in 2025, 5,000 in 2024 and 12,000 in 2023. However, when presenting such figures on successful crossings, the ministry does not indicate how it calculates them, given that successful crossings are often inherently undetected. Most of those who manage to cross do not remain in Poland, instead heading westwards, in particular to Germany. “The statistics clearly show that the 3 billion zloty (€692 million) investment in the security of the Polish-Belarusian border has delivered the intended results – we are effectively protecting our country from illegal migration organised by the Belarusian regime with the support of the Kremlin,” declared the ministry. Poland says that “specialists from the Middle East” have been brought to Belarus to dig tunnels under the border for migrants to cross into Poland. Four such tunnels have been discovered this year, including one last week that was used by 180 migrants https://t.co/4ConkQnj8z — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 16, 2025 Among the measures taken to protect the border are a 5.5-metre-high steel fence as well as an electronic monitoring system that detects attempts to cross and dispatches officers to the scene. In 2024, following the death of a soldier who had been stabbed by a migrant attempting to cross the border, Poland also loosened the rules on the use of firearms by officers posted there. Since last year, it has banned asylum claims by people who cross from Belarus. Last August, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen visited Poland’s border with Belarus, where she thanked the Polish authorities for defending Europe from “cynical hybrid attacks” orchestrated by Belarus and Russia. Germany’s interior minister, Alexander Dobrindt, also praised Poland’s “impressive” efforts “to stop illegal migration” and said that it was vital for the EU to offer financial and logistical support. EU chief @vonderleyen has thanked Poland for defending Europe from “cynical hybrid attacks” during a visit with PM @donaldtusk to the border with Belarus. Last week, Latvian interior minister Jānis Dombrava told Euronews that his country has now “become the main target” for Belarus’s migrant trafficking, instead of Poland and Lithuania. On Thursday, Latvia recorded 111 attempted illegal crossings from Belarus, compared to two in Lithuania on the same day and zero in Poland the previous day. Poland has cautiously welcomed an announcement by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky of a five-point plan intended to alleviate the diplomatic crisis triggered by his earlier decision to name a military unit after the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), which led massacres of Poles during World War Two. In a statement on Friday evening, Zelensky announced that, following a meeting on Kyiv’s policy towards Poland, “the priorities are clear: all of us in Europe need good-neighbourly, equal, and mutually beneficial relations built on respect”. He reiterated Ukraine’s gratitude for Poland’s “significant support” since Russia’s full-scale invasion and announced that his administration had “agreed on several key steps” in response to the current tensions. I held a meeting on our policy toward Poland. The priorities are clear: all of us in Europe need good-neighborly, equal, and mutually beneficial relations built on respect. Poland provided significant support to Ukraine after the start of Russia's full-scale invasion, and we are… pic.twitter.com/5dNFQYqi1n — Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) July 17, 2026 “First, there will be decisions on the diplomatic track,” said Zelensky, though without indicating what this would mean in practice. “Second, all archives of the Security Service of Ukraine and the Foreign Intelligence Service of Ukraine concerning the tragic events in Volyn during the 20th century will be opened.” The latter is a reference to the historical issues that are at the heart of the dispute. The historical region of Volhynia, which is now mostly in Ukraine, was part of Poland in the interwar period. There, and in some neighbouring areas, the UPA, a nationalist partisan formation, led massacres of around 100,000 Polish civilians, mostly women and children, during World War Two, when the region was under Nazi-German occupation. Poland recognises those massacres as a genocide. Ukraine vehemently rejects that label, and also points to anti-Ukrainian measures in the region by the interwar Polish state as well as massacres of Ukrainians by Polish groups during the war. As his third pledge, Zelensky announced that there would be “decisions to grant a substantial number of permits for search and exhumation work”. From 2017 to 2025, Ukraine prohibited searches for and exhumations of Polish massacre victims on its territory, where it is believed that tens of thousands remain buried in unmarked mass graves. In a diplomatic breakthrough, such work was allowed to resume last year. However, Ukraine has so far only approved a small number of requests for searches and exhumations, prompting some complaints from Poland. Poland has for the first time used DNA testing to identify the remains of Poles massacred by Ukrainian nationalists in WWII. “After more than 80 years, families are receiving the answer they have awaited for generations,” says the culture minister https://t.co/c1gM3kQ83s — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 14, 2026 As a fourth point, Zelensky said that his team had “discussed possible formats for expanding dialogue between the societies of Ukraine and Poland”, though again without providing details as to what this would involve. Finally, he said that he had agreed with the head of the Ukrainian Institute of National Remembrance (UINP), Oleksandr Alfyorov, to expand the institute’s capabilities and funding, so that it can “properly represent Ukraine’s interests”. Alfyorov caused anger in Poland earlier this year when he said that the Volhynia massacres are viewed in Ukraine as “just a local historical episode” and suggested they did not constitute a genocide. That prompted a rebuke from Poland’s own Institute of National Remembrance (IPN). Poland's state historical institute has criticised remarks by the head of its Ukrainian counterpart about massacres of Poles by Ukrainians in WWII. He said they are regarded in Ukraine as a "local episode" and suggested they do not constitute a genocide https://t.co/MAi6RhpRDL — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 11, 2026 In response to Zelensky’s announcement, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that he “accepted the words and decisions with satisfaction and hope”. He reiterated that Poland is “ready for a serious and friendly dialogue on the matters that unite us and those that divide”. However, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, a deputy prime minister, emphasised that it was important now for “the announcements regarding the opening of archives, exhumations and dialogue to turn into concrete actions”. “Today, Poland and Ukraine have a common enemy: Russia,” added Kosiniak-Kamysz. “That is where the threat lies. Sowing discord between our nations serves the interests of the Kremlin.” Z satysfakcją i nadzieją przyjmuję słowa i decyzje @ZelenskyyUa, dotyczące relacji między naszymi państwami, które muszą być oparte na wzajemnym szacunku i prawdzie. Jesteśmy gotowi do poważnego i przyjaznego dialogu w sprawach, które nas łączą i tych, które nas dziś dzielą. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) July 17, 2026 Meanwhile, a senior aide to Polish President Karol Nawrocki – who deepened the crisis by last month stripping Zelensky of Poland’s highest honour – also cautiously welcomed Zelensky’s announcement. “Facing the historical truth is the only way to build further relationships,” Bartosz Grodecki, the head of Nawrocki’s National Security Bureau (BBN), told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). “The Ukrainian president’s decision to open the entire archives of the Security Service of Ukraine and the Foreign Intelligence Service of Ukraine concerning the events in Volhynia, as well as additional permits for search and exhumation work, is a step in this direction,” he added. Long-simmering tensions between Poland and Ukraine over WWII massacres have finally boiled over, prompting a diplomatic crisis.@danieltilles1 looks at how we got here and what it may mean for the two countries and Europe more broadly https://t.co/a8tiYJJHRr — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 22, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland up 30% this year
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland was 30% higher in the first half of this year compared to the same period in 2025, newly reported police data show. The figures come following a number of recent high-profile cases of verbal and physical attacks against Ukrainians – who are Poland’s largest immigrant group – as well as ongoing diplomatic tensions between Kyiv and Warsaw. 🔴Coraz więcej ataków na Ukraińców w Polsce – wynika z danych @PolskaPolicja https://t.co/6ZnKFILbdL — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) July 17, 2026 The new data, which were reported by the Rzeczpospolita daily, show that police received 180 reports of hate crimes against Ukrainians in the first half of 2026, which was around 30% higher than in the same period last year and around 35% more than in 2024. If the same trend continues, there would be around 360 such reports by the end of the year, more than the 275 recorded in 2025 and 267 in 2024. However, Rzeczpospolita notes that the figures relate to reported incidents of hate crimes, rather than confirmed cases. On the other hand, experts point out that many such incidents are never even reported to the police. “It is generally assumed that hate crimes are underreported,” Jacek Kucharczyk, head of the Institute of Public Affairs, a think tank, told the newspaper. “Some victims don’t want to report a crime because they’re simply afraid.” Ukrainians are by far Poland’s largest foreign national group, with around 1.6 million living in the country. While Poland welcomed Ukrainian refugees in 2022, there has been growing negative sentiment towards them recently, indicated in polls and through anti-Ukrainian rhetoric from prominent politicians. In particular, two far-right opposition parties, Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), have used anti-Ukrainian rhetoric, while the largest opposition group, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has recently taken a tougher line towards Ukraine. Kucharczyk told Rzeczpospolita that the “toxic atmosphere” around Ukrainians is now spreading from political rhetoric into real-life consequences, as seen in the new police data. He added that Russia also seeks to stoke and exploit such sentiment. An 18-year-old Ukrainian will stand trial in Poland accused of working on behalf of Russia to stir tension between Poland and Ukraine by painting dozens of inscriptions in public places glorifying the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, which massacred Poles in WWII https://t.co/0w0gVYiGpp — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 16, 2026 In May, five Polish teenagers were detained in Warsaw over a violent attack on a group of young Ukrainians. The city’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, blamed the anti-Ukrainian rhetoric of right-wing politicians for “encouraging thugs” to carry out these kinds of attacks. Tensions with Ukraine have since ramped up even further, amid a diplomatic dispute sparked by President Volodomyr Zelensky’s decision to name a military unit after a Ukrainian nationalist group that led massacres of Poles during World War Two. Earlier this month, two Polish far-right activists were charged over an incident in which they confronted a Ukrainian woman who runs a business that offers assistance to other Ukrainian immigrants. Last week, a man was detained after being recorded hurling xenophobic obscenities at Ukrainian children on a bus in the city of Bielsko-Biała. That latter incident prompted Ukraine’s foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, to call on “Polish politicians to stop inciting hatred against Ukrainians”. Ukraine’s foreign minister has called on "Polish politicians to stop inciting hatred against Ukrainians” after an incident in which a man was filmed shouting xenophobic obscenities at Ukrainian girls on a bus in Poland. The perpetrator has been detained https://t.co/AfGCNqtJbj — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 13, 2026 Figures from Poland’s government, which is a coalition ranging from left to centre right, have also condemned recent incidents of hate towards Ukrainians. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called last week’s incident in a bus “disgusting” and warned of the potential “disastrous consequences” of inciting national hatred. Interior minister Marcin Kierwiński promised that the state would deal with “any form of aggression”, but also blamed the right-wing opposition for stirring antipathy. However, PiS spokesman Rafał Bochenek accused the government of “cynically exploiting” the incident in Bielsko-Biała “for political purposes”. He said it was, in fact, Tusk and Kierwiński who were “responsible for the brutalisation of public life in Poland”. Meanwhile, Ukraine’s ambassador to Poland, Vasyl Bodnar, hailed the fact that “the entire political class” in Poland had condemned the incident on the bus and expressed hope that the recent wave of attacks is a “temporary symptom” that “will pass”, reports the Polish Press Agency (PAP). Two Polish far-right activists have been charged over an incident in which they confronted a Ukrainian woman who runs a business providing services to immigrants. One of the two men was separately charged this year with espionage on behalf of Russia https://t.co/SdhlXUhym2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 10, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: President vetoes legal rights for same-sex couples in Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, has vetoed a government bill that would have allowed unmarried partners, including same-sex couples, to sign an agreement granting them certain rights. The proposed law would have marked the first time that Poland had recognised same-sex relationships in domestic law. However, Nawrocki argued that such a move would threaten the institution of marriage, which is enshrined in the constitution. The measures in question were approved by both houses of parliament in May and June with the support of Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right. The proposed law would have allowed couples, both same-sex and opposite-sex, to enter into a new type of contract, signed before a notary and then submitted to the registry office. It would have granted them some of the rights available to married couples, including joint property and tax settlement, access to their partner’s medical information, exemption from inheritance and gift taxes, and the right to decide about their partner’s burial if they died. However, the two main opposition parties – the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) and far-right Confederation (Konfederacja) – voted against the legislation, and Nawrocki himself also made clear that he intended to veto it. The government’s majority in parliament has approved a bill that would grant same-sex partners some of the rights available to married couples. However, President Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, has made clear he will veto the law https://t.co/hx8viUN6QH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 29, 2026 On Friday morning, the president confirmed he would not be signing into law the two bills passed by parliament that would have introduced the new system. He said that the measures would effectively “introduce civil partnerships through the back door”, and that such partnerships are “intended to replace or substitute the institution of marriage”. “As the guardian of the constitution, I cannot accept a solution that would lead to the loss of the special status of marriage defined in article 18 of the constitution as a union between a woman and a man, placed under the protection and care of the Republic of Poland,” he added. Nawrocki also argued that the proposed measures were contrary to the principles of social justice because they would have granted such couples some of the privileges of marriage but without all of the same obligations. He also noted that the proposed new type of contract could be terminated far more easily than a marriage. “Marriage, which best secures family stability, cannot become one of many equally valid options offered by the state administration,” declared the president. “The family is a community fundamental to the survival of the nation.” However, Nawrocki added that, as he has previously said, he remains open to legislation that would grant loved ones rights relating to healthcare and various administrative issues. But only if it “does not create an alternative to marriage” or “introduce ideological changes to family law”. Poland has begun recognising foreign same-sex marriages. But the legal consequences for such couples remain unclear, especially as Polish law does not allow any form of same-sex union We asked five experts for their view on what this will mean in practice https://t.co/h2KHmW8sMI — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 19, 2026 Nawrocki’s decision was condemned by Tusk, who called it “an expression of contempt toward people and their right to happiness and a normal life”. The government’s plenipotentiary for equality, Katarzyna Kotula, accused the president of “turning his back on the two million Poles living today in informal relationships”. However, she pledged that “the veto will not halt social change”. If such change “cannot go through the door, then [it will go] through the window”. Kotula noted that Poland has already begun legally recognising same-sex marriages conducted in other European Union member states, after being ordered to do so by the European Court of Justice. While “not all benefits are yet available” to such couples, “this is something that I intend to deliver”, she added. Prezydenckie weto to wyraz pogardy wobec ludzi i ich prawa do szczęścia i normalnego życia. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) July 17, 2026 However, the government’s ability and willingness to take such action, even when it cannot be vetoed by Nawrocki, is hampered by internal disagreements over the issue within Tusk’s coalition. The Left (Lewica), from which Kotula hails, and Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party are generally in favour of strengthening LGBT+ rights. But they have met with resistance from more conservative elements in the coalition, in particular the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL). The measures vetoed today by Nawrocki were already a compromise within the government: earlier plans to introduce same-sex civil partnerships were watered down to instead simply allow same-sex couples to sign a contract granting them certain rights. However, opinion polls show that the Polish public itself is in mostly in favour of recognising same-sex relationships. State research agency CBOS last year found its highest-ever level of support for the introduction of civil partnerships, with 62% of Poles in favour. State research agency @CBOS_Info has found its highest-ever level of support in Poland for the introduction of same-sex civil partnerships. Over 62% are now in favour, up from 52% last year and just 25% in 2011, when the question was first asked https://t.co/Y9ydpbwsoU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 14, 2025 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Ukrainian teen indicted by Poland for working on behalf of Russia to stir historical tensions
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish prosecutors have indicted an 18-year-old Ukrainian accused of working on behalf of Russia to stir tensions between Poland and Ukraine by painting dozens of slogans in public places glorifying the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), which massacred Poles during World War Two. Among the sites where he placed graffiti were a monument to Polish victims of those massacres (pictured above), as well as a memorial dedicated to the heroes of the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising. If found guilty, the suspect could face up to life in prison. The history of the UPA has been at the heart of an ongoing diplomatic dispute between Warsaw and Kyiv. However, the actions in this particular case took place in 2024 and 2025, before the current crisis emerged. Prokurator z dolnośląskiego wydziału PZ PK skierował do Sądu Okręgowego we Wrocławiu akt oskarżenia przeciwko Illii K., któremu zarzucono popełnienie 47 przestępstw związanych z działalnością dywersyjną i sabotażową na rzecz obcego wywiadu. 45 zarzutów dotyczy umieszczania na… — Prokuratura (@PK_GOV_PL) July 16, 2026 The suspect in the case was detained in August 2025, shortly after graffiti glorifying the UPA had appeared on a monument in Poland honouring victims of the so-called Volhynia massacres, in which the UPA led the slaughter of around 100,000 Poles. On Thursday, prosecutors announced that they have issued an indictment against the suspect, whom they named only as Illia K. under Polish privacy law. He is accused of 47 crimes in total. Of those, 45 are for “acts of subversion and sabotage for the benefit of foreign intelligence, consisting primarily of writing slogans in Ukrainian on the facades of buildings and in memorial sites with the text ‘Glory to the UPA’ and red-and-black flags attributed to the UPA “, prosecutors said. Those actions “were aimed at inciting hatred on national grounds, deepening antagonisms between Poles and Ukrainians, causing social unrest and creating a sense of helplessness of state authorities”. There have long been tensions between Poland and Ukraine over the massacres, which Poland recognises as a genocide. Ukraine rejects that label, and also continues to honour the UPA for its role in fighting for independence from Moscow-backed Soviet rule. The issue has recently flared up again after President Volodymyr Zelensky in late May named a Ukrainian military unit after the “heroes of the UPA”. That sparked widespread anger in Poland and prompted Polish President Karol Nawrocki to strip Zelensky of his country’s highest honour. Russia has also long sought to exploit such tensions, and Poland’s Internal Security Agency (ABW) notes that Illia K.’s actions were carried out “at the request of the Russian security services”, which were seeking to “incite conflicts between the Polish and Ukrainian nations”. Russia has published purported archival documents relating to massacres of Poles by Ukrainians in WWII. Kyiv had warned that Russia was planning to release the files in order to stir tensions, while Polish media note that the material contains nothing new https://t.co/CI0cfAlDle — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 6, 2026 In addition, Illia K. also faces one charge of participation in an organised criminal group and another of preparing for an act of subversion or sabotage that would have involved flying a drone over Poland’s Armed Forces Day parade in Warsaw last year, which was attended by President Nawrocki. Prosecutors note that the accused “acted for financial, not ideological, reasons”. He was paid for his actions in cryptocurrencies. That is typical of the so-called “disposable agents” Russia increasingly uses, who are amateurs – often young Ukrainians or Belarusians – hired and paid through messaging service Telegram. The suspect has been held in pretrial detention since he was arrested by the ABW last year. If found guilty, he could face up to life in prison. Prosecutors say that, although Illia K. initially admitted to the charges against him, he later decided to change his stance and has pleaded not guilty while exercising his right to remain silent. The head of Poland's security services has appealed to Ukrainians, the country's largest immigrant group, not to be tempted to earn money by acting as Russian agents. Russia regularly recruits Ukrainians in Poland to carry out espionage and sabotage https://t.co/aa5UUWWBrx — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 28, 2025 Poland has in recent years detained, charged and in some cases convicted dozens of agents accused of carrying out espionage, sabotage and other so-called “hybrid actions” on behalf of Russia and its ally Belarus. In March, the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism (ICCT) reported that Poland is now the “primary focus of Russian activity” when it comes to sabotage. In June, foreign minister Radosław Sikorski warned that Moscow is “waging a full-scale cognitive war against us” and that there is a “Russian fifth column” operating in Poland. Russia is “waging a full-scale cognitive war against us”, Polish foreign minister @sikorskiradek has warned. He also said that there is a “Russian fifth column” operating in Poland https://t.co/wsmZSvYnzN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 9, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Volkswagen hires 100 sheep to cut grass at Polish solar farm as experiment in agrivoltaics
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Carmaker Volkswagen has deployed a herd of 100 sheep to keep grass under control at a solar farm that powers one of its factories in Poland, providing a greener alternative to mechanical mowing. The project, which is being run in partnership with a local university, will also contribute to research on agrivoltaics, the name given to the use of land for both solar generation and agriculture. Scientists will assess the impact of the practice on animal welfare and the wider ecosystem. In 2016, Volkswagen opened a major plant near Poznań, Poland’s fifth-largest city. The facility employs around 3,000 people and mainly produces VW’s Crafter van. In 2023, the company opened a solar farm next to the plant. On sunny days, its 31,000 photovoltaic panels can power the whole factory, though over the year as a whole it supplies around 25% of its electricity. Volkswagen has now announced that, earlier this year, it welcomed around 100 sheep to the solar farm. They are grazing on the 27 hectares of land around the panels as an alternative to mechanical mowing. “The animals adapted very well to the new conditions,” says Justyna Nowak-Gajek, the owner of the flock. She explains that the sheep are splitting into smaller groups and “grazing peacefully”, whereas herds that feel unsafe tend to stick closer together. Meanwhile, scientists from the Poznań University of Life Sciences (UPP) are studying the impact of the project on the animals’ welfare and behaviour, as well as the functioning of the entire ecosystem. “We are checking, among other things, whether shade created by the panels reduces heat stress in animals, improving their comfort and living conditions,” says Joanna Składanowska-Baryza from the university’s Faculty of Veterinary Medicine and Animal Sciences. “At the same time, we are analysing changes in the microclimate, vegetation and soil to identify solutions that facilitate the effective combination of energy production with agricultural activities.” Volkswagen has chosen Poland as the location for a new €1.7bn plant producing materials for electric vehicle batteries. The investment has been welcomed by the Polish government, which is providing €350 million in grants for the project https://t.co/xh0LuzHOyq — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 10, 2023 The study is expected to inform the wider practice of agrivoltaics, which aims to “create [solar] installations that coexist with their surroundings and bring additional benefits to the environment and local communities”, says Quanta Energy, the firm that constructed Volkswagen’s solar farm. “The photovoltaic farm now produces more than just green energy,” adds Marzena Pillich-Grońska, director of the Volkswagen plant. “It has also become a place where we support biodiversity, local agriculture, and the development of scientific knowledge.” In recent years, a number of Polish cities, including Kraków and Katowice, have also recruited sheep and goats as a greener alternative to mechanical cutting of grass on municipal land. Various firms operating in Poland have been investing in renewables to supply themselves with energy. In 2024, the largest chocolate maker in Poland, Mondelez Polska, said it would spend $1 million (3.8 million zloty) on solar installations at its production sites in the country. Successive Polish governments have also been seeking to bolster green energy. Last year, the country generated 29.4% of its electricity from renewables, up from 9.4% a decade earlier. Onshore wind led the way with 14.2%, followed by solar at 12.1% and biomass at 1.8%. However, in 2023, a group of business associations and international companies, including Google, Amazon, Mercedes and Ikea, warned the government that there must be more rapid development of green energy in order to attract continued investment in Poland. However, since then, figures show a period of stagnation, despite the current government pledging to accelerate Poland’s green transition after taking power from its conservative predecessor in 2023. World.title: Senior official under former Polish government detained over media campaign that attacked judges
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A former senior official under the Law and Justice (PiS) government that ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023 has been detained and charged as part of a probe into the alleged misspending of funds. The case relates to the activities of the Polish National Foundation (PFN), a body created by PiS to promote Poland abroad. However, it spent 8.4 million zloty (€1.9 million) on an advertising campaign in Poland itself that promoted the PiS government’s controversial judicial reforms. 🛑 Dzisiaj rano na polecenie prokuratora Prokuratury Regionalnej w Rzeszowie agenci Centralnego Biura Antykorupcyjnego zatrzymali dwóch byłych członków Polskiej Fundacji Narodowej: 64-letniego Macieja Ś. i 63-letniego Cezarego J. 🛑 Śledztwo jest prowadzone w sprawie nadużycia… — Jacek Dobrzyński (@JacekDobrzynski) July 14, 2026 On Tuesday, the spokesman for Poland’s security services, Jacek Dobrzyński, announced that a 64-year-old, who can be named only as Maciej Ś. under Polish privacy law, had been detained. Maciej Ś. was a board member of the PFN at the time that the spending in question took place in 2017. Later, in 2022, he was appointed by PiS as the head of the National Broadcasting Council (KRRiT), a state media regulator, a position he held until 2025. Dobrzyński revealed that another former member of the PFN board, Cezary J., had also been detained as part of the same investigation into abuse of power and failure to fulfil duties. The spokesman noted that the allegations relate to the PFN’s so-called “Fair Courts” campaign, which he said “caused material damage to the foundation on a massive scale, in an amount of no less than 8.4 million zloty”. The PFN was established under the PiS government in 2016 by 17 state-owned companies, which provided funds for it to promote Poland abroad. However, the following year it launched the “Fair Courts” campaign, in which billboards and other forms of advertising in Poland were used to show the alleged failings of the justice system in Poland and therefore to justify why reforms being implemented by PiS were necessary. Echoing PiS rhetoric, the campaign suggested that judges saw themselves as a “special caste” and highlighted cases of alleged wrongdoing by individual judges, including one who had been caught stealing a sausage. (The judge in question had not ruled on a case since that incident in 2006 and had died in 2015.) In 2018, a Warsaw court ruled that the “Fair Courts” campaign was inconsistent with the PFN’s statutory goals, saying that not only did the adverts fail to enhance Poland’s image abroad, “on the contrary, they significantly weakened it, creating a negative image of the judiciary based on individual cases”. “The ‘Fair Courts’ campaign primarily involved attacking the judicial community,” said Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of the security services, commenting on Maciej Ś.’s arrest. “This campaign responded to a political order from the PiS government and discredited independent courts.” “The financial damage to the foundation amounted to at least 8.4 million zloty, while the moral damage is incalculable,” he added. “The use of the foundation’s funds for partisan purposes must be accounted for.” On Tuesday evening, prosecutors announced that they had charged Cezary J. That was followed on Wednesday morning by news that Maciej Ś. had likewise been charged and banned from leaving the country, reports the Polish Press Agency (PAP). CBA na polecenie prokuratury zatrzymało Macieja Ś. i Cezarego J., którzy jako członkowie zarządu Polskiej Fundacji Narodowej uruchomili w 2017 środki fundacji na kampanię "Sprawiedliwe Sądy", polegającą przede wszystkim na atakowaniu środowiska sędziowskiego. Ta kampania… — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) July 14, 2026 The “Fair Courts” campaign was just one of a number of controversial initiatives launched by the PFN under the PiS government. The foundation was regularly accused of spending money to support PiS’s political goals or on seemingly wasteful projects. One of its most famous initiatives involved the purchase of a yacht for almost €1 million, which was renamed “I Love Poland” and sent on an around-the-world cruise to mark the centenary of Poland’s independence in 2018 (though it suffered damage and spent weeks stuck in a port, accruing further costs). In 2021, the Supreme Audit Office (NIK) accused the PFN of violating the law by refusing to provide documents required for an audit. In February 2025, just over a year after PiS lost power, a newly appointed PFN board accused its predecessors of criminal negligence that caused damages of over 30 million zloty to the foundation’s finances. They notified prosecutors of potential crimes. World.title: Five Legendary Ballets in One Night at Prague’s Hybernia Theatre
World.content:
Prague’s Hybernia Theatre is hosting a series of special evenings dedicated to classical ballet, bringing together some of the most celebrated scenes from the world’s best-known productions.

The upcoming Classic Ballet Gala will take place on July 22, 25 and 29.

More info about the program here.

The performance will feature students and graduates of the conservatory, presenting excerpts from legendary ballets including Don Quixote, Swan Lake, The Nutcracker, Sleeping Beauty and Le Corsaire.

Rather than focusing on a single full-length production, the gala will offer audiences the opportunity to experience highlights from several major works in one evening.

The young dancers will perform in specially prepared costumes and under the guidance of experienced teachers, including former soloists of the National Theatre Ballet. The artistic concept and dramaturgy of the evening are overseen by Pamela Morávková and Jiří Horák.

The programme will combine the dramatic energy of Don Quixote, the romantic atmosphere of Swan Lake, the fantasy world of The Nutcracker, the fairy-tale elegance of Sleeping Beauty, and the adventure of Le Corsaire.

Founded in 1945, the Prague Dance Conservatory is the oldest and largest institution of its kind in the Czech Republic. Over eight decades, the school has educated generations of dancers, choreographers, ballet masters and teachers who have performed on stages in the Czech Republic and abroad.

Its students regularly take part in international competitions and represent Czech dance at festivals and cultural events around the world.

World.title: Look Up! JAS 39 Gripen Jets to Fly Over Prague on Wednesday
World.content:
Prague residents will have the chance to see JAS 39 Gripen fighter jets flying above the city on Wednesday, July 22.

The aircraft will take part in a ceremonial event at the National Memorial on Vítkov.

The flyover is scheduled for 11:30 a.m. and will be carried out as a training flight connected with the ceremony.

According to information from Prague 4 City Hall, the jets will approach the capital from the east, flying over areas including Běchovice, Dolní Počernice and Žižkov.

The aircraft will then turn south over Prague Castle before continuing their return route through Podolí, Nusle and Hostivař. After completing the flight over the city, the jets will head back to their base in Pardubice.

The route means residents in several parts of Prague may be able to see the aircraft, depending on weather conditions and visibility.

Military aircraft flights over the capital are relatively rare but not unusual. In March 2024, crowds gathered in central Prague to watch a large military flyover marking the 25th anniversary of the Czech Republic joining NATO.

That event included five fighter jets and an Airbus aircraft, which flew over landmarks including Charles Bridge. The fighter jets later returned to their bases, while the Airbus landed at Prague’s Václav Havel Airport.

The Czech Air Force regularly uses ceremonial flights to mark important national events and military anniversaries, while also serving as training exercises for pilots.

World.title: Twelve Prague Tram Lines Changed Due to Repairs in City Center
World.content:
Tram services on Spálená Street and Národní třída in central Prague have been suspended due to track repairs.

The closure, which began on Saturday, will continue until August 10 and affects 12 tram lines operating through the city center.

The Prague Public Transit Company (DPP) has not introduced replacement bus services during the disruption. Passengers are advised to use the metro as an alternative, especially for journeys through the busiest parts of the city.

The affected section runs between the Újezd and Lazarská stops and impacts tram lines 2, 4, 5, 9, 18, 22, 23, 42, 93, 97, 98 and 99.

Several routes have been temporarily modified. Some trams are being redirected through the National Theatre stop on Masarykovo nábřeží, while others are operating via Myslíkova Street and Jiráskovo náměstí, or through Anděl and Švandovo divadlo. Some lines have received more significant route changes.

Two Temporary Tram Lines Added During Repairs

To help manage the disruption, DPP has introduced two temporary tram services.

Line 32 connects Vypich with Sídliště Řepy, while line 39 runs between Vozovna Žižkov and Náměstí Bratří Synků.

A new temporary stop has also been created at Malostranská. During daytime operations, trams will stop on the Edvarda Beneše embankment in the direction of Čechův most. During night service, the stop will operate on Letenská Street in both directions.

Track Repairs Include New Switches and Overhead Line Upgrades

The ongoing construction focuses on replacing worn sections of the tram infrastructure at the intersection of Spálená and Lazarská streets.

Workers will also repair track curves, install two new grease traps near the Máj department store, modernize two tram switches and replace aging overhead line poles near the National Theatre.

Additional local repairs to the tram network will also be carried out during the closure period.

World.title: Why Film Fans Traveled Hundreds of Kilometers to See “The Odyssey” in Prague
World.content:
Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey attracted film fans from across Europe to Prague, where Cinema City Flora hosted a sold-out 70mm IMAX premiere.

Tickets for the opening night sold out within hours of going on sale, with visitors traveling from several countries to experience the film as Nolan intended.

The adaptation of Homer’s ancient epic has been among the year’s most anticipated releases since its announcement. While its cast and source material generated significant attention, much of the excitement centered on its technical achievement.

The Odyssey is the first feature film shot entirely on 70mm IMAX film, making screenings in compatible theaters exceptionally rare.

Cinema City Flora is among roughly four dozen cinemas worldwide equipped to project 70mm IMAX film. Until earlier this month, it was the only venue in continental Europe with that capability.

Following the opening of new theaters in France and Belgium, it is now one of just three across mainland Europe still offering the format. It also remains the continent’s longest-operating 70mm IMAX venue.

Because 70mm IMAX projectors are no longer manufactured and require specialized maintenance, very few cinemas can continue operating the technology.

That scarcity has turned Prague into a destination for moviegoers willing to travel hundreds, and in some cases thousands, of kilometers to see major releases in their original presentation.

Set after the conclusion of the 10-year Trojan War, the story follows the hero Odysseus (Matt Damon) as he returns to Ithaca, a journey that takes nearly as much time as the war.

Borrowing from the Greek tradition of oral storytelling, Nolan’s nearly three-hour adaptation is told through the accounts of a bard (played by Travis Scott) who spins tales of the great warrior and Odysseus himself as he reflects on the events of his homecoming voyage.

World.title: Two Dead After Axe and Knife Attack at Prague Hostel
World.content:
Two people died and another person was seriously injured after a violent axe and knife attack at a hostel in Prague.

Police officers responding to the scene shot and killed the attacker, who had also threatened them.

The incident happened on Thursday evening at a hostel on Vídeňská Street in Prague 4, according to Czech news outlet Novinky.cz, which first reported on the case.

The hostel is located near the Institute of Clinical and Experimental Medicine (IKEM), and the attacker and victims were reportedly employees of the medical facility.

Police said the suspect attacked people inside the building before turning on responding officers. The officers used their weapons against him, and the attacker was killed at the scene. Authorities later confirmed that no further threat to the public remained.

Emergency crews treated four people following the incident. Two victims suffered cardiac arrest and rescuers immediately began resuscitation efforts. Despite their attempts, both patients died.

A third person suffered serious injuries caused by a sharp weapon. After receiving medical treatment, the injured person was transported to a trauma centre while conscious.

The fourth person involved in the incident was not physically injured but required medical attention due to psychological and internal complications, according to emergency responders.

Police continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the attack, including the motive of the suspect.

World.title: A Night with Mozart: Candlelit Concert and Fine Dining in Historic Ballroom
World.content:
Few cities are as closely connected to Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart as Prague.

More than two centuries after Don Giovanni premiered here, visitors can still experience his music in a setting that captures the atmosphere of the era.

The Mozart Dinner at the Grand Hotel Bohemia combines a live opera performance with a three-course dinner in the hotel’s spectacular Boccaccio Hall, one of Prague’s finest historic ballrooms.

The concert features leading opera singers accompanied by a string quintet, performing some of Mozart’s best-known arias and duets from The Marriage of Figaro, The Magic Flute, and Don Giovanni.

The latter holds a special place in Prague’s history, having premiered at the city’s Estates Theatre in 1787.

The performance is designed to be more intimate than a traditional opera concert. Instead of remaining on stage throughout the evening, the singers move through the hall, performing among the audience and making guests feel part of the experience.

The evening is divided into three musical performances, with each followed by a course of dinner. Rather than separating the concert from the meal, the format allows the two to complement one another, creating a relaxed pace that encourages guests to enjoy both.

The menu draws on traditional Czech and Austrian cuisine, reflecting the region’s culinary heritage while matching the historic surroundings.

Each course has been carefully selected to accompany the evening without distracting from the music.

World.title: Prague 6 Wants to End Night Flights from Václav Havel Airport by 2032
World.content:
Prague 6 is calling for a complete ban on night flights at Václav Havel Airport, arguing that residents should have the right to uninterrupted sleep.

The district wants to gradually reduce air traffic during nighttime hours, with a full restriction planned no later than 2032.

The airport currently plans to limit night operations to 48 flights per night under its voluntary declaration. However, Prague 6 officials say the number is still too high and want stricter measures.

“Our goal is to ensure that residents of Prague 6 can enjoy peaceful and undisturbed sleep, which is a basic condition for a healthy and fulfilling life in our district,” said Prague 6 Mayor Jakub Stárek (ODS).

The district council is seeking a complete ban on flights between midnight and 5:30 a.m. by 2032. According to officials, the measure would significantly reduce noise exposure and improve the quality of life for people living near the airport.

The district plans to negotiate the proposal with Air Traffic Control, the national Slot Coordination Office, and the Ministries of Transport and Finance. A special working group is expected to be created to discuss possible solutions.

Prague 6 wants the number of night flights to decrease by at least 20 percent every year starting in 2027. Under this plan, nighttime operations would gradually disappear by 2032, except in emergency situations or other extraordinary cases.

However, Prague Airport has previously said that a complete shutdown of night operations is currently not possible due to capacity reasons. Similar restrictions are already in place at some European airports, including those in Frankfurt and Vienna.

Airport says it has already reduced noise impact

Prague Airport says it has already taken several steps to reduce the impact of aircraft noise on surrounding communities.

According to its environmental declaration, annual traffic has fallen from around 178,000 flights in 2008 to approximately 140,000 flights in 2025, mainly due to the increased use of larger aircraft. The airport has also restricted access for noisier aircraft categories during nighttime hours and currently coordinates only 48 flights between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.

Runway closure has increased noise complaints

The debate over aircraft noise has intensified after the main runway at Václav Havel Airport was temporarily closed for construction and technical upgrades. The closure, scheduled until mid-August, has forced aircraft to use the secondary runway.

As a result, flight paths have shifted over different parts of Prague, including densely populated areas. Many residents have complained about increased aircraft noise.

World.title: Meet the Czech Superfan Who Dedicated His Home to Messi and Maradona
World.content:
In the quiet village of Bukovka, around 90 kilometres east of Prague, one house stands out from all the others.

Painted in Argentina’s iconic sky blue and white, complete with a giant Sun of May on its façade, it is impossible to miss. Outside, a life-sized statue of Diego Maradona greets visitors, while a massive mural of Lionel Messi and Argentina’s 2022 World Cup-winning squad covers the back of the building.

The extraordinary home belongs to Miloslav “Čurby” Urbanec, 51, arguably Czechia’s most devoted supporter of Argentine football.

Urbanec’s passion began almost five decades ago. As a four-year-old, he watched the 1978 FIFA World Cup with his father, who supported Brazil. But while his father admired Pelé and the Brazilian greats, Urbanec fell in love with Argentina.

The team’s long-haired stars reminded him of Winnetou, his childhood hero, and Argentina’s triumph that summer sealed a lifelong obsession.

His admiration has since grown far beyond simply watching matches. After returning from the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, he decided to transform his property into a tribute to Argentina’s football culture.

The mural features not only Lionel Messi but also head coach Lionel Scaloni, assistant coaches Pablo Aimar and Walter Samuel, and every member of the World Cup-winning squad.

Behind the house lies another remarkable feature: a private five-a-side football pitch inspired by Boca Juniors’ famous La Bombonera stadium. What was once an unused, swampy area has been converted into a miniature arena complete with terraces that can accommodate around 50 spectators.

The surrounding fences are decorated with images of Boca Juniors legends, reflecting Urbanec’s deep affection for Argentina’s most famous club.

The football theme extends to almost every corner of his life. His van is painted in Argentina’s colours and features images of Maradona lifting the World Cup alongside the slogan “In Messi We Trust.” One of his sons is named Lionel, while his attempt to name another child Diego Armando was politely vetoed by his wife.

Inside the house, Urbanec keeps an extensive collection of football memorabilia, including around 50 shirts from Argentine clubs, vintage editions of the legendary magazine El Gráfico, signed photographs and posters of both Maradona and Messi.

As Argentina prepare to face Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, the blue-and-white house in Bukovka is once again ready to celebrate. For Urbanec, another World Cup dream is just one match away.

World.title: Trump warns Iran over US troop deaths
World.content:
US President Donald Trump said Monday that Iran will pay “many times over” for any American troops killed amid ongoing hostilities in the Middle East.

Pentagon: three US deaths over the weekend

“Every time Iran kills an American Soldier they will pay for that killing many times over,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

This directive has been passed on to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Daniel Caine, and “every Leader in the Military,” Trump added.

The statement came as the US continued to carry out airstrikes against Iran, with the attacks largely focused on southern Iran. Tehran retaliated with strikes targeting facilities and bases that it says are used by the US military in several regional countries, Anadolu said.

The Pentagon confirmed three US deaths over the weekend, including two at a military base in Jordan and one in northern Iraq.

The exchange of fire between the two countries comes despite a Pakistani-brokered memorandum of understanding signed in June to end the war and reach a lasting peace deal.​​​​​​​

According to a report by CNN, the US and Iran have considered a 10-day ceasefire to halt hostilities in an effort to prompt a return to negotiations, with the cessation in violence also including lifting restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz.

The White House said that diplomacy was proceeding along with efforts to make Iran “pay” for the recent deaths of US soldiers.

“Right now, President Trump is focused on making Iran pay for their violations of the MOU (memorandum of understanding) and their continued acts of terrorism in the Strait of Hormuz,” a US official said.

“In addition, the president will make Iran pay for the recent deaths of U.S. soldiers,” the official said. “These devastating blows will continue until the president deems otherwise, but talks between our countries are continuing.”

Trump says Netanyahu ‘will not be arrested’ in US

In a separate post, Trump said that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu “will not be arrested, in any way, shape, or form, while in the United States of America.”

“He is fighting against the Islamic Republic of Iran, which recently killed 52,000 innocent protestors, and has spent the last 47 years killing American Soldiers, and others,” Trump added.

“The only ones that should be arrested are the people that led Iran into this unprecedented spiral of death and destruction, something that should have been dealt with years ago, by previous Presidents.”

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has told The New York Times that his administration’s legal department is actively discussing the potential arrest of Netanyahu.

“I believe that Prime Minister Netanyahu belongs in The Hague,” Mamdani said. “He’s a war criminal who has been charged by the International Criminal Court. And what you will find is that is an opinion that is held by many purely because of what his actions have wrought over these last many years.”

Netanyahu recently postponed a US visit originally set for this month to September.

World.title: PM Péter Magyar regrets Judit Polgár’s decision but accepts it ‘with respect’
World.content:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar said he regretted Judit Polgár’s decision not to accept a potential presidential nomination but would respectfully acknowledge it. He also took personal responsibility for communication mistakes surrounding the selection process.

Magyar published a video statement on Facebook on Monday evening after holding talks with Polgár, whom he described as “a living legend of Hungary”.

According to the prime minister, the chess grandmaster told him that, considering the circumstances surrounding the proposed nomination, she would not stand for the presidency.

“I am sorry, but I respectfully acknowledge her decision,” Magyar said.

He added that millions of Hungarians would probably agree that the country would have gained an exceptional opportunity had Judit Polgár agreed to serve as head of state.

Magyar praised her knowledge, international reputation, humanity and patriotism, arguing that these qualities could have made her an outstanding president.

Magyar says Judit Polgár acted responsibly

The prime minister said Polgár’s refusal itself demonstrated that she would have been suitable for the position.

In his assessment, she had carefully considered the weight of the office, including its personal and public consequences, before reaching a clear and honest decision.

Magyar thanked Polgár for taking the proposal seriously and praised the openness, directness and dignity with which she handled the situation.

Following their conversation, he said he respected her even more because she had shown responsibility, restraint, humanity and commitment to Hungary.

“Judit Polgár’s life, achievements and service to Hungary are an example to all of us,” the prime minister said.

Polgár, widely regarded as the strongest female chess player in history, announced earlier on Monday that she did not feel she had sufficient strength to assume the historic responsibility of uniting a divided nation. She nevertheless promised to support a future independent and respected president.

Prime minister accepts responsibility for communication mistakes

Magyar also addressed the criticism surrounding the speed and handling of the attempted nomination.

He apologised if communication errors caused by his enthusiasm and complete confidence in Polgár had contributed to the situation or influenced her decision.

“The responsibility lies solely with me,” he said.

The proposed nomination had prompted criticism from politicians, analysts and civil society organisations. Some argued that the process appeared rushed and did not provide enough time for meaningful public discussion.

Magyar acknowledged that events had not unfolded in a manner everyone would regard as correct or ideal. However, he argued that no selection process could gain the support of every citizen.

He said the government and the governing Tisza Party would learn from both their mistakes and the experience.

Read Hungary’s most important news in English every evening in one place: 

Tisza to continue searching for Hungary’s next president

Magyar insisted that the government had requested recommendations from political parties, public figures, civil organisations and private citizens from the beginning of the process.

He said Polgár had been proposed by respected representatives of Hungary’s cultural, scientific and sporting communities, while several other public and confidential recommendations had also been received.

The prime minister contrasted this process with previous presidential selections, which he claimed had been decided through agreements between political parties. This was Magyar’s political characterisation of the earlier procedure.

Under the current transitional rules, Hungary’s National Assembly will elect a president to serve until a new constitution is adopted. Magyar said the Tisza parliamentary group was expected to meet several times during the week to assess the proposed candidates before submitting its nomination to parliament.

According to the prime minister, Tisza will support a candidate who can represent the entire nation, possesses authority based on personal achievement and remains independent of party-political conflicts.

He said the party would not back anyone who had played a prominent role as an MP, minister or senior partisan figure during the divisive political decades preceding the 2026 change of government.

Magyar concluded that Hungary needed a president capable of bringing estranged social groups closer together after decades of political confrontation.

The search will therefore continue for a candidate whose integrity, judgement, patriotism and public service are recognised across political divisions.

World.title: Who is “Magyar”? The Ukrainian drone commander Russia has learned to fear
World.content:
Robert Brovdi, better known by his military call sign “Magyar”, has become one of the best-known commanders in Ukraine’s drone war against Russia. In recent weeks, his unit—known as Magyar’s Birds—has claimed a series of unprecedented strikes against Russia’s so-called shadow fleet in the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov, disrupting fuel deliveries to occupied Crimea and drawing growing international attention.

Why is he called “Magyar”?

Before becoming one of Ukraine’s most prominent military commanders, Robert Brovdi was a businessman. He was born in Ukraine into the country’s Hungarian minority in Transcarpathia (Zakarpattia), a region bordering Hungary that has long been home to a sizeable ethnic Hungarian community. His Hungarian heritage earned him the call sign “Magyar”—the Hungarian word for “Hungarian”—which he has carried throughout his military service, 24.hu said.

Following Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, Brovdi volunteered for military service and quickly became one of the pioneers of Ukraine’s drone warfare. What started as a small volunteer drone team evolved into Magyar’s Birds, one of Ukraine’s most effective unmanned aerial units. He now commands Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces, overseeing increasingly sophisticated long-range drone operations.

How did Magyar’s Birds become famous?

Initially, the unit gained attention for using inexpensive commercial drones to destroy Russian tanks, artillery systems and troop positions with remarkable precision.

Over time, the force expanded into a highly specialised drone formation capable of coordinating large-scale operations involving reconnaissance drones, first-person-view (FPV) attack drones and long-range strike systems.

The unit regularly publishes combat footage that has attracted millions of views online and helped establish Magyar as one of the public faces of Ukraine’s rapidly evolving drone warfare.

The campaign against Russia’s shadow fleet

The latest operation has brought Brovdi’s unit into the international spotlight.

According to Ukrainian military statements, Magyar’s Birds have participated in coordinated attacks against Russia’s so-called shadow fleet—a network of ageing tankers and cargo vessels used to transport Russian oil despite Western sanctions.

💥 Seven Russian shadow fleet vessels hit overnight in the Black and Azov Seas According to Robert Brovdi ("Madyar"), commander of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces, three oil tankers and four cargo ships were targeted overnight. In total, 183 vessels have been hit in July as… pic.twitter.com/xpHHvdSmdl — NEXTA (@nexta_tv) July 20, 2026

According to Reuters, between early and mid-July, Ukrainian officials said the operation disabled more than 150 vessels in the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea. Rather than sinking ships outright, the drones reportedly targeted propulsion and steering systems, leaving vessels unable to operate while avoiding major oil spills. Reuters reported that the objective was to paralyse maritime logistics supplying occupied Crimea rather than destroy ships outright.

If you missed it: Suspected Russian operatives held at Hungarian border ‘may have been plotting bombing in Germany’ — authorities tight-lipped

Why does the shadow fleet matter?

Russia’s shadow fleet has become a crucial tool for maintaining oil exports despite sanctions imposed after the invasion of Ukraine.

Many of the vessels operate under opaque ownership structures, frequently changing names, flags and insurers to evade restrictions. Disrupting these shipping routes can complicate fuel deliveries to Crimea and increase Russia’s dependence on road and rail logistics, which are themselves vulnerable to Ukrainian strikes, Reuters said.

A symbol of Ukraine’s drone warfare

Whether viewed as a military innovator or simply one of Ukraine’s most recognisable commanders, Robert “Magyar” Brovdi has become closely associated with the country’s transformation into a global leader in drone warfare.

His operations illustrate how relatively low-cost unmanned systems can threaten infrastructure and logistics once thought to be beyond the reach of conventional battlefield tactics, making “Magyar’s Birds” one of the most closely watched military units in the war today.

World.title: BREAKING! Judit Polgár rejects Péter Magyar’s offer to become Hungary’s president
World.content:
Hungarian chess legend Judit Polgár has declined Prime Minister Péter Magyar’s invitation to become the country’s next president, saying she did not feel strong enough to take responsibility for uniting a deeply divided nation.

Polgár announced her decision in a Facebook post on Monday evening, shortly after Magyar personally approached her about taking on the largely ceremonial but symbolically important position.

The grandmaster described the proposal as one of the greatest honours of her life and praised the prime minister for seeking an independent candidate despite the governing Tisza Party’s decisive parliamentary majority.

However, she ultimately concluded that she could not accept the position.

“I do not feel that I have enough strength to assume the historic responsibility of uniting a divided nation,” Polgár wrote, adding that she was therefore unable to accept the invitation.

Polgár promises to support an independent president

Although Polgár rejected the role, she said she remained committed to the goals associated with the nomination.

She pledged to support a new president who is independent, widely respected and capable of representing Hungarians across political divisions.

“I will do everything in my power to support a new, independent and recognised president in achieving these goals,” she wrote.

Magyar responded to the decision in a comment addressed directly to the chess champion.

The prime minister thanked Polgár for everything she had done for Hungary and said the country would continue to count on her contribution in other ways.

“Perhaps I can say on behalf of many millions of Hungarians that, even if in a different form, we will continue to count on you in the future,” Magyar wrote.

Reports of Polgár’s decision were published by several Hungarian news outlets on Monday evening.

Why Péter Magyar approached the chess grandmaster

The search for a new head of state began after President Tamás Sulyok signed Hungary’s 17th constitutional amendment on Saturday. The measure brought his presidential mandate to an early end on 20 July.

Sulyok had been elected by parliament in 2024, during the government of former prime minister Viktor Orbán. His removal formed part of a wider series of institutional changes introduced by Magyar’s Tisza government following its election victory in April 2026.

Parliamentary Speaker Ágnes Forsthoffer has taken over the presidential responsibilities on an interim basis while the government and parliament seek a permanent successor.

As we wrote today, two women temporarily take the country’s top constitutional posts

Magyar had promised broad public consultation on the identity of the next president. On Sunday, several well-known figures from Hungary’s cultural, scientific and sporting communities proposed Polgár as a candidate.

The prime minister subsequently announced that he would meet her and ask whether she was prepared to serve as president until the adoption of a new constitution. The parliamentary group of the governing Tisza Party also unanimously backed her potential nomination on Monday.

Read Hungary’s most important news in English every evening in one place: 

There was no public support behind it

The day after the heads of government made their announcement, Europion conducted a nationally representative survey involving 1,800 respondents regarding the nomination of Judit Polgár as head of state. The results are presented in the charts attached below; our main findings are as follows:

Among the population aged 16 and older, 35% oppose and 26% support Judit Polgár’s nomination for head of state. Opponents are primarily those over 60 (47%), those without a high school diploma (38%), and Fidesz voters (58%), while support significantly exceeds the national average among college graduates (33%) and Tisza voters (38%).

It is clear that the decision even divides Tisza Party voters: 38% support it, but 24% oppose it.

A significant portion of the public is taking a wait-and-see approach: 17% gave a neutral (3) rating, while an additional 23% were unable or unwilling to take a position on the issue, or are unfamiliar with Judit Polgár.

A relative majority of Hungarians (38%) tended to agree with the criticism that Judit Polgár “has no politically relevant knowledge or experience, and this is, after all, a political position,” while only 20% identified with the narrative that “Judit Polgár is a widely recognized, successful figure who stands apart from party politics, and therefore will be able to embody national unity.” Among Tisza voters, the situation is reversed: in this group, 30% tend to identify with the supportive narrative.

Nearly as many (27%) expect Judit Polgár to be “an independent head of state who does not shy away from conflict” as those (31%) who expect her to be “a more accommodating, conflict-avoiding head of state.”

Prime Minister Péter Magyar announced that he will ask Judit Polgár to serve as head of state until the new Constitution takes effect. Do you support this decision? (Population aged 16 and older, %):

A globally recognised Hungarian figure

Judit Polgár is widely regarded as the strongest female chess player in history. She became a grandmaster at the age of 15 and was the only woman to break into the top ten of the overall world rankings.

Unlike many leading female players, Polgár primarily competed in open tournaments rather than women-only competitions. During her career, she defeated several world champions and reached a peak world ranking of eighth.

Her international reputation, political independence and achievements outside party politics had made her an attractive potential candidate for a presidency expected to represent national unity.

Her refusal means the Hungarian government must now continue its search for a new head of state. The identity of the next candidate, as well as the timetable for the parliamentary election, has not yet been announced.
